title: Watch the Input, Not the Representation: A Frozen One-Byte Token as an Independent Silent-Failure Runtime Monitor for AI Models
abstract: Watch the Input, Not the Representation: A Frozen One-Byte Token as an Independent Silent-Failure Runtime Monitor for AI Models Randolph James Ferlic, M.D. and Kimberly Kate Ferlic — Fieldstone Analytics, LLC, Austin, TX, USA Preprint · Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23351878 · CC-BY 4.0 · Community: spiral-domain-encoder-campaign · a characterization of previously filed and published methods; no new algorithmic subject matter is disclosed. Abstract A companion deposit established that a frozen, deterministic, class-discriminant single-token encoder's label-free nearest-centroid novelty score can serve as an independent competence-boundary interlock for an industrial decision model. This paper asks the AI-safety question directly: can that one-byte monitor guard a model — detecting when the model has entered territory where it can no longer be trusted — and where in the pipeline should it watch? We test it, pre-registered, as a runtime monitor across twenty probes in four batteries (AI-safety, hardening, frontier, and foundation-model/realism). Eleven confirmed, nine refuted — each refutation into a sharper statement. Silent-failure early warning. Under progressive input shift the monitor's trip rate tracks the guarded model's error at Spearman +0.99 and leads it — it trips on 61% of inputs while the model is still 99.4% accurate, firing before accuracy collapses (on real structural drift it saturates to a binary shift alarm rather than grading the harm). A value-adding diverse channel. The independent novelty monitor and the model's own confidence catch partially-disjoint failures, so their union covers 0.987 of failures versus 0.91 for either alone (cross-domain the gain is a modest few points) — the defense-in-depth case that an area-under-curve tie cannot make. Watch the input, not the representation (the central finding). Running the monitor on a trained network's embeddings is never better and usually worse than on the input: out-of-distribution detectability falls monotonically with how much a representation is shaped by the task — input area-under-curve 0.82 ≈ random projection 0.82 > unsupervised autoencoder 0.76 > discriminative shallow 0.75 > discriminative deep 0.74 (Spearman shaping↔area-under-curve −1.00); it is supervised shaping, not depth, that erases the signal, since a random deep network preserves it. Input-space detection is at parity with a standard autoencoder reconstruction-error detector and a standard two-sample shift test — the one caveat being that 'the input' must be an informative representation, not raw samples. Learned representations hide what inputs reveal. Breadth and backdoors. The monitor extends to vision (handwritten-digit open-set area-under-curve 0.92) on the separability law, and detects additive backdoor triggers down to small magnitudes (0.49 at a 0.25-σ trigger), with a genuinely on-manifold backdoor remaining the honest blind spot. A genuine pretrained foundation model's embedding (Chronos-T5) is itself a poorer monitoring space (0.85) than domain input features — generic pretraining is uninformative for a specialized failure — and that deficit is governed by the program's separability law, not model choice: kNN-purity rank-predicts monitoring area-under-curve across all four representation spaces (Spearman +1.00), with the foundation embedding lowest on both (a small residual below the strict line is the honest caveat). The monitor meets deployment realities: a 10% human-review budget catches 88% of out-of-distribution inputs, and gating cuts a safety-critical cost four-fold. The thesis is a deployable design rule for AI-safety runtime monitoring: a cheap, deterministic, auditable, independent monitor should watch an AI model's inputs — it is a silent-failure early-warning and a diverse defense-in-depth layer, and it is explicitly not a semantic judge of the model's outputs nor a solution to alignment. No new algorithmic subject matter is disclosed; the monitor is the program's filed label-free novelty score, the guarded models and attacks are standard, all measured on public data. Highlights · A one-byte runtime monitor for AI models. Silent-failure early-warning (trips before accuracy collapses, Spearman +0.99) and a diverse defense-in-depth channel (union coverage 0.987 vs 0.91), reading inputs only — deterministic, auditable, independent of the guarded model. · Watch the input, not the representation. OOD-detectability falls monotonically with task-shaping (Spearman −1.00); learned representations discard OOD information (feature collapse), so a discriminative activation monitor reads a space from which the danger has been partly erased. Input-space detection matches a standard autoencoder detector. · Honest throughout. Six of eleven pre-registered hypotheses refuted into sharper statements; the monitor watches a distribution, not a meaning — not a semantic guardrail, not an adversarial defense, not alignment. · Breadth. Extends to vision and the common additive-backdoor threat; the on-manifold blind spot and drift-sensitivity recur as the consistent boundary. · Foundation-model era. A genuine pretrained foundation model's embedding (Chronos-T5) is a worse monitoring space than domain features (0.85 vs 0.97) — uninformative for a specialized failure — so don't monitor foundation embeddings; and that deficit is itself rank-predicted by the program's separability law (Spearman +1.00 across spaces, foundation embedding lowest on both), not an accident of model choice. The monitor meets EU AI Act Art. 14 (a 10% review budget catches 88% of OOD) and cuts safety-critical cost 4×. · No new IP. The monitor is the program's filed label-free novelty score; the guarded models and attacks are standard; measured on public data. What this record contains · Manuscript_Paper61.pdf — the runtime-monitor characterization (7 figures, 36 references); and Manuscript_Paper61.docx, the editable source. · PAPER_61_ZENODO_ARCHIVE.zip — the reproducibility archive (md5 in ARCHIVE_MD5.txt): the frozen pre-registration (AISAFETY_PREREG.md: the six-probe AI-safety battery AS-1..5/AS-4b, the five-probe hardening battery AH-1..5, the four-probe frontier battery FH-1..4, and the foundation-model/deployment-realism battery FM-1/HO-1/FM-2, with their bands); the five runners (the AI-safety battery, the hardening battery, the frontier battery, the foundation-model/realism battery, and the separability-law-on-the-foundation-embedding probe); the shared dataset loaders and the frozen token encoder; the result records (JSON); the seven figures and their builder; the manuscript source; and a README. Public data is not redistributed (two rolling-element bearing corpora, an aircraft-handling gesture corpus, a smartphone human-activity corpus, a thirty-six-month chemical gas-sensor-array drift corpus, and two image corpora — optical handwritten digits and faces; each read from a local cache at run time, and the foundation-model probe reads a pretrained time-series foundation model via its standard library and cached weights); all paths and handles are scrubbed and leak-scanned, and the productization know-how — the per-deployment configuration-selection and commissioning procedure — is retained privately and excluded (the monitor is characterized with the plain labeled novelty score and a percentile threshold). evidence.title: Watch the Input, Not the Representation: A Frozen One-Byte Token as an Independent Silent-Failure Runtime Monitor for AI Models

Abstract A companion deposit established that a frozen, deterministic, class-discriminant single-token encoder's label-free nearest-centroid novelty score can serve as an independent competence-boundary interlock for an industrial decision model. This paper asks the AI-safety question directly: can that one-byte monitor guard a model — detecting when the model has entered territory where it can no longer be trusted — and where in the pipeline should it watch? We test it, pre-registered, as a runtime monitor across twenty probes in four batteries (AI-safety, hardening, frontier, and foundation-model/realism). Eleven confirmed, nine refuted — each refutation into a sharper statement. Silent-failure early warning. Under progressive input shift the monitor's trip rate tracks the guarded model's error at Spearman +0.99 and leads it — it trips on 61% of inputs while the model is still 99.4% accurate, firing before accuracy collapses (on real structural drift it saturates to a binary shift alarm rather than grading the harm). A value-adding diverse channel. The independent novelty monitor and the model's own confidence catch partially-disjoint failures, so their union covers 0.987 of failures versus 0.91 for either alone (cross-domain the gain is a modest few points) — the defense-in-depth case that an area-under-curve tie cannot make. Watch the input, not the representation (the central finding). Running the monitor on a trained network's embeddings is never better and usually worse than on the input: out-of-distribution detectability falls monotonically with how much a representation is shaped by the task — input area-under-curve 0.82 ≈ random projection 0.82 > unsupervised autoencoder 0.76 > discriminative shallow 0.75 > discriminative deep 0.74 (Spearman shaping↔area-under-curve −1.00); it is supervised shaping, not depth, that erases the signal, since a random deep network preserves it. Input-space detection is at parity with a standard autoencoder reconstruction-error detector and a standard two-sample shift test — the one caveat being that 'the input' must be an informative representation, not raw samples. Learned representations hide what inputs reveal. Breadth and backdoors. title: A reason with the switch: what an agent memory pipeline passes on when fallback runs come with a stated purpose. Protocol and materials frozen before the run (Paper 7, Study 2)
abstract: Frozen protocol, code and materials of the second study of a paper on what LLM agents' memory-writing pipelines keep from a run of tool outcomes, deposited before any smoke or confirmatory model call (the manifest's OpenTimestamps proof is included; its Bitcoin attestation is checked by the gated launcher). The first study (frozen and deposited as doi:10.5281/zenodo.23291437) found, descriptively, that after nine successes of a standard route and two runs on a fallback that the scripted agent made without a stated reason, almost every session reading the summaries of a replay of the memory pipeline of OpenAI's open-source Codex agent (default v1 instructions, pinned at commit ecebd679; an adapted replay, not the shipped pipeline) chose the fallback for the next run. This study gives the two fallback runs a reason in their requests (none; a bare request for the fallback; a dated check of the fallback set on the calendar before the runs; a permanent move to it), on the first study's 96 streams, and compares what fresh sessions reading the replay's summaries, a run log carrying the requests, or a record of per-route counts choose and forecast for the next run. The registered contrasts set the bare request against the dated check under the v1 summaries, the v1 summaries against the log under the check, and the two changes against each other; no choice is scored. The archive holds the registration (REGISTRATION.md), the design memos, the study's code, which runs the first study's frozen files, unchanged in their bytes, on the new tree (replacing some of their functions as they are loaded, as the registration states), every file of the first study that it executes or reads (byte-identical to the first study's freeze manifest, which the code checks at import), the request notes and the codebook of the two model coders, the coder pilot's gates and summary, the power, size and spend tables, the wave-1 writer schedule, the pre-freeze reviews of the design and of the package with their dispositions, and the chain scripts. MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file with its SHA-256; MANIFEST.sha256.ots is its OpenTimestamps proof. Manifest SHA-256: 0d381d9e5fcd48a3f53138d4185283e2cf2014ea59490f02cd9d528ed9b5abdb. Zip SHA-256: 3fd7ccbcc2e90c3dec2622724e9bf879d30e9119775c1621997d6e4d7ca0f399. No result of this study is included. Licences: paper7/study2/LICENSE.md and, for the first study's files, paper7/study1/LICENSE.md.

title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-Evolving Coding Agent For Physical Intelligence
abstract: Coding agents can construct executable programs and revise them through feedback, offering a foundation for embodied control without target-task fine-tuning. Through a programmatic robot interface, the agent observes the scene, executes control programs, and adapts them to the resulting physical state, serving as the closed-loop policy. However, this within-episode adaptation does not automatically preserve experience across scenes. Our trajectory analysis shows that agents spend interaction and inference budgets establishing effective operations and identifying their preconditions, while fresh agents cannot reuse these discoveries. This motivates EmbodiedEvo, a self-evolving coding agent that distills physical feedback into reusable code Skills and diagnostic Lessons. Experience is acquired on one Playground scene per task, then frozen for independent agents in unseen scenes, without updating model weights. On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

title: What Makes a Good Visual Representation for Spatial Understanding in MLLMs?
abstract: Spatial understanding is a necessary step in moving multimodal large language models (MLLMs) toward reasoning about the 3D physical world. Their visual pretraining data, however, is almost entirely 2D, so the visual tokens processed by MLLMs often lack inherent 3D structural information. A growing number of methods inject such structure by transferring representations from external vision or geometry models, and collectively establish that such transfer helps. Behind these methods lies a largely underexplored question: what makes a visual representation good for spatial understanding? To answer it, we first separate what is transferred from how it is transferred, and then trace the resulting differences back to properties of the representations themselves. What we transfer comes from 3D geometry models, self-supervised image and video models, vision-language models, and generative models, in the form of latent features or explicit depth and point maps. We transfer it either by distillation, using it as a supervision target, or by fusion, feeding it as an additional input. We find that a representation's 3D structure correlates strongly with how much it helps, measured by cross-view consistency for latent features and by depth and reconstruction accuracy for explicit geometry. We further show that the form of a representation dictates the mechanism it needs. Latent features gain as much from fusion as from distillation; explicit geometry gains little from fusion, and most of its distillation gain depends on a geometry decoding head. Guided by these findings, we distill both latent features and explicit geometry into a single MLLM. Taking only RGB video as input, it consistently improves over its base model on both static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning benchmarks.

title: GLST: Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Memory Decomposition Framework for Online Chained-Goal Navigation
abstract: Autonomous navigation in real-world environments often requires long-horizon operation under partial observability and evolving goals. Existing mapless navigation approaches predominantly assume fixed goals throughout an episode, limiting applicability to practical scenarios where goals change online during execution. We study online chained-goal navigation, where goals evolve through existing-goal redirection or new-goal emergence without explicit transition signals. Under this setting, we find navigation may require either continued exploration or strategic revisitation, creating conflicting memory requirements. We propose Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Belief Learning (GLST), a memory-decomposition framework that separates latent beliefs into global-local spatial and long-short temporal representations for long-horizon reasoning. We further introduce goal-conditioned rewards to balance exploration and exploitation under evolving goals. Extensive experiments in simulation across diverse terrains demonstrate improved chained-goal navigation performance over baselines. Real-robot experiments using the Spot quadruped further validate our memory decomposition framework.

title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control and no mechanism against the geographic dropout that non-uniform cloud cover leaves behind. We present Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), an algorithm that treats building a co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a hemisphere-corrected (class x season x region) stratification, enforces strict temporal pairing and a multi-stage quality gate, and closes the loop during acquisition with a human-in-the-loop deficit-repair stage. Measured on its own product, the algorithm yields three results a single-pass acquisition cannot report. Deficit-driven ordering makes a partial run a covering one: it holds every one of the 192 strata populated from the first few percent of the budget, where an abundance-first order leaves most strata empty until the end. Whether a failed attempt can be recovered depends on the temporal persistence of its cause, not the kind of defect: geometric failures such as nodata are among the most repairable (eta = 41.4%) while cloud is among the least (eta = 18.8%), because a cloudy location is cloudy on most dates of its season. The repair loop supplies 39.5% of the released pairs at no measurable quality cost, with 89.8% surviving manual review. The quality guarantee has a price: 2,928,370 acquisition attempts produced 740,746 released pairs. We release the corpus, STRATA-S12, with STAC/PDS4-aligned FAIR sidecars, and a pre-registered linear-probe check confirms it is fit for self-supervised pre-training. A metadata-level coverage comparison against SSL4EO-S12 and SEN12MS situates the corpus over a shared frame; systematic cross-corpus and cross-method comparison is left to follow-up work.

title: Dynamic safety filters in reinforcement learning for robotic systems
abstract: Pri spodbujevalnem učenju se agent uči iz lastnih poskusov in postopno izboljšuje svojo strategijo, torej pravilo, ki vsakemu stanju priredi dejanje. V robotiki je tako učenje drago, saj napaka lahko pomeni poškodbo robota in tveganje za okolico. Nevarnost se običajno rešuje s statičnimi pravili, na primer s pragom na kotu, ta pa ne upoštevajo dinamike fizičnih sistemov: isti kot je lahko povsem varen ali že nepopravljivo izgubljen, odvisno od smeri gibanja in preostalega nadzora. V delu preizkušamo dinamično alternativo, pri kateri agent nevarnost oceni sam, brez zunanje opredelitve prepovedanih stanj. Osrednja mera je opolnomočenost: koliko različnih prihodnjih izidov lahko agent s svojimi dejanji še doseže, zato upade, ko agent izgublja nadzor. Oceno z utežjo prištejemo k nagradi za nalogo kot pomožno nagrado, tako da se agent uči tudi ohranjati nadzor. Za primerjavo vključimo še prediktivno informacijo, ki meri, koliko prihodnosti je mogoče razbrati iz preteklosti. Mehanizem preverjamo na determinističnem obrnjenem nihalu, ki ga mora agent z omejenim navorom pripeljati v ukazano lego in jo zadržati. Z vzvratno dosegljivostjo je mogoče za vsako stanje natančno izračunati, ali je padec, torej prekoračitev mejnega kota, ki konča epizodo, še mogoče preprečiti. To služi kot referenčna resnica o tveganju, delež učnih epizod s padcem pa kot merilo varnosti učenja. Učimo tako strategije za posamezen cilj kot eno strategijo za vse cilje. Analiza približno 3.000 učnih tekov prinese tri ugotovitve. Prvič, opolnomočenost tveganje zares zaznava: stanja razvrsti po nevarnosti občutno bolje kot katerakoli od obeh spremenljivk, iz katerih je izračunana (rangovna korelacija z izračunano referenco 0,70 proti 0,33 za kotno hitrost in 0,00 za kot nihala), prediktivna informacija pa na istem preizkusu odpove. Drugič, vpliv uteži ni sorazmeren kompromis, temveč ima optimum: pri zmernih vrednostih se padci med učenjem občutno zmanjšajo ob komaj opaznem upadu uspešnosti naloge, pri pretiranih pa pomožna nagrada prevlada nad nalogo in agent cilj opusti. Tretjič, pri strategiji za posamezen cilj korist ne izvira iz vsebine signala, saj jo enako dobro dosežeta kontroli brez informacijske vsebine, konstantna in naključno premešana pomožna nagrada. Pri enotni strategiji za vse cilje pa opolnomočenost korist obdrži in padce med učenjem zniža s 43,8 na 27,7 %, obe kontroli pa sta slabši od izhodišča brez pomožne nagrade. Notranji varnostni signal je torej učinkovit le, kadar je porazdelitev obiskanih stanj dovolj široka, da signal preko nje ohrani dovoljšnjo variabilnost

title: Haxion - r home computer system
abstract: *Current Security Posture of Haxion + Glyphon* We have built a deliberately hostile environment for unauthorized control: - Custom language (Glyphon) with ritualized safety invocations - Mandatory authority levels and authentication (including backslang) - Cryptographic script signatures - Independent safety microcontroller that the main OS cannot override - One-way telemetry only - Built-in antiviral scanning + scrubber - Persistent locked configuration - Tamper-evident audit log - Dry-run / simulation mode under restricted authority - Sensor plausibility checks and graceful degradation This makes opportunistic and remote attacks extremely difficult. The system is intentionally alien to normal tooling and forces any attacker into expensive, targeted work. It is *highly secure by design* for its intended use. It is not magic and still requires good physical security and supply-chain discipline. --- What would you like to do next? 1. Formal threat model (what we defend against well vs residual risks) 2. Kernel-side implementation outline for the antiviral + scrubber 3. More Glyphon examples (emergency, degraded mode, multi-script) System Integration Summary: Drone & Video Uplink Addendum We have officially appended a high-bandwidth real-time data uplink and drone video ingest channel to the Mnemosyne Procurement Model. This integration specifically bridges the physical, safety-first computing layer of GlyphonOS with the primary Mnemosyne intelligence framework. rainos was taken so we are glyphon os

title: A TYPOLOGY-INFORMED METHODOLOGICAL MODEL FOR BUILDING AN UZBEK–CHINESE PARALLEL CORPUS
abstract: Uzbek and Mandarin Chinese lie at opposite ends of the morphological spectrum: Uzbek is an agglutinative Turkic language with SOV order and a rich case system, whereas Chinese is an isolating Sino-Tibetan language with SVO order, function words and numeral classifiers, written without word boundaries. Our search did not identify a systematic, openly available Uzbek–Chinese parallel corpus; the only directly relevant study found builds a filtered, partly LLM-generated pseudo-parallel dataset from news crawls. This paper proposes a typology-informed methodological model for building such a corpus. It has five components: (1) a layered design separating a human-verified gold core, an automatic extension and a labelled synthetic layer, with provenance metadata; (2) asymmetric linguistic processing linked through Universal Dependencies; (3) multi-level alignment down to the morpheme, with correspondence-type labels; (4) a "unit–set of equivalents" lexical database; and (5) retrieval-augmented integration with large language models. A correspondence table and two author-composed sentence pairs show that most grammatical correspondences are not one-to-one. An evaluation protocol is specified for future empirical work.

title: A Python Laboratory for Private Synthetic Data and Privacy Models
abstract: This program demonstrates DataSynthesizer's PrivBayes, SmartNoise Synth's MST and AIM, and OpenDP's central counting and local randomised-response mechanisms using a fictional health survey. It generates synthetic records, evaluates selected statistical relationships and subgroup errors, and illustrates how trust assumptions differ between central, local and shuffle models. Public categorical domains control preprocessing, while meaningful checks verify output validity, encoding consistency and estimator behaviour. The shuffle demonstration permutes existing randomised reports without claiming an amplified privacy guarantee. The laboratory includes version reporting and example outputs; its exact diagnostic comparisons are intended for fictional data and are not automatically safe to release for confidential datasets.

title: An Investment Analysis Research Enhanced Enterprise Development Algorithm for Bankruptcy Prediction
abstract: Corporate bankruptcy prediction requires reliable optimization methods capable of identifying effective machine-learning configurations while maintaining robust global search performance. This study proposes an investment-analysis-inspired Enhanced Enterprise Development Optimizer (EED) for global optimization and KNN-based bankruptcy prediction. Rather than introducing additional generic perturbation operators, EED incorporates historical performance appraisal, covariance- and correlation-based search allocation, and drawdown-aware adaptive recovery into the original Enterprise Development Optimizer. The optimization performance of EED is evaluated on the CEC2017 and CEC2022 benchmark suites under five dimensional settings and compared with eleven competing algorithms. For CEC2017, F2 is excluded because of documented implementation inconsistencies and unstable numerical behavior, and the remaining 29 functions, namely F1 and F3–F30, are used in the evaluation. Each algorithm is independently executed 30 times, and the results are assessed using the mean and standard deviation, convergence and distribution analyses, the Friedman rank test, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. EED achieves the best or tied-best mean performance on 28, 27, and 23 of the 29 retained CEC2017 functions at 30, 50, and 100 dimensions, respectively, and on 9 and 8 of the 12 CEC2022 functions at 10 and 20 dimensions. Its overall Friedman mean rank is approximately 1.41, while the Wilcoxon comparison with the original ED yields 107 wins, 3 ties, and 1 loss, indicating that the proposed mechanisms provide consistent improvements across different benchmark landscapes rather than gains on only a small number of functions. To examine practical applicability, EED is further used to optimize the neighborhood size and distance measure of KNN on the Wieslaw and JPNBDS bankruptcy datasets. The resulting EED-KNN models show competitive and relatively stable performance in ACC, MCC, F1-score, and precision. The benchmark experiments therefore establish the general search capability and robustness of EED, while the bankruptcy-prediction application demonstrates that these optimization advantages can be transferred to a discrete machine-learning parameter-selection task.

title: Why Static Skill Inconsistencies Do Not Equate to Runtime Risks: A Behavioral Analysis of LLM Agent Execution
abstract: LLM agent frameworks heavily rely on external skill assets to standardize tool usage, encode operational workflows, and supply executable runtime resources. Despite their widespread adoption, multi-component skill packages frequently suffer from cross-artifact inconsistencies, where documentation, scripts, and configuration files specify conflicting behavioral constraints. Although static auditing techniques can uncover such contractual discrepancies, static defect volume cannot reliably reflect real-world agent performance degradation. This gap leaves practitioners without rigorous evidence to assess the practical risk of flawed agent skills. This paper presents a systematic empirical study to demystify the runtime implications of skill inconsistencies. We conduct large-scale auditing over 575 community and benchmark skills, yielding 1,182 manually validated contract inconsistencies. We further build a controlled evaluation pipeline with 49 executable agent tasks and three representative LLMs across NoSkill, OriginalSkill, and FixedSkill experimental settings. Through fine-grained behavioral analysis of 441 paired execution trajectories, we quantify the actual performance impacts of resolved defects.

title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
abstract: Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. Scaling collection across diverse environments, in turn, favors lightweight, portable capture systems. Yet, existing datasets provide only partial views of this coordination. Thus, we introduce EgoExplorer, a 100-hour vision-motion-touch observatory of human loco-manipulation built with a wearable system. With an emphasis on professional activities, its continuous recordings align egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, fine-grained finger articulation, and tactile observations, accompanied by step-level descriptions. To achieve this coverage with sparse body sensing, we develop the Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline. Concretely, reusable calibration fixes participant geometry and sensor attachments before motion inference to disentangle mounting offsets from articulation. A temporal prior then completes unobserved joint motion, while layered constraints promote measurement agreement, temporal continuity, and geometric consistency, properties that motion plausibility alone does not guarantee. Against tracker-fitted references, the method reduces body-point error by 71.9% relative to the strongest baseline; matched evaluations also show gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning alongside humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.

title: Autonomous Cyber Operations Gym for Training and Evaluating AI Models for Defence
abstract: This paper proposes an Autonomous Cyber Operations (ACO) gym, a unified framework integrating high-fidelity network emulation, realistic user behaviour modelling for benign network traffic and adversarial profiles, and the generation of cybersecurity scenarios through open toolkits. By supporting live and deferred feature extraction at the packet and flow levels, the gym facilitates the creation of labelled synthetic datasets for training Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs), as well as developing and evaluating modular components for autonomous defence agents through emulated interactions. While evaluation of a DNN classifier within the gym shows high in-domain performance, achieving near-perfect recall on adversarial network flows, our experiments reveal a significant sensitivity to domain shift, showing that even minor changes in network composition, such as variations in traffic protocol distribution, can lead to a catastrophic collapse in model transferability and detection performance.

title: Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning Based Voice Conversion for Electrolaryngeal Speech Enhancement
abstract: Electrolaryngeal (EL) speech suffers from severe acoustic mismatches with normal speech, resulting in degraded naturalness and intelligibility. These mismatches also make sequence-to-sequence voice conversion struggle to learn robust intermediate representations, hindering EL-speech-to-normal-speech conversion (EL2SP) performance. To address this, we propose a novel multimodal contrastive representation learning framework to 1) achieve richer multimodal-representation learning, and 2) facilitate the transferability of multimodal representations to speech-only EL2SP. First, EL speech and text representations are fused to learn multimodal representations for target speech generation, during which cross-modal contrastive learning is employed to encourage a semantically consistent speech--text representation space. Next, the fused representations are treated as a fixed target to guide speech-only representation learning through cross-stage contrastive learning, enabling multimodal knowledge to be transferred to the EL2SP task while preserving architectural and inference simplicity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms both the speech-only and multimodal-based baselines.

title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
abstract: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/

title: Workflow implementations in applications with MCP and large language models
abstract: V zaključnem delu je obravnavana implementacija delovnih tokov v aplikacijah s pomočjo protokola Model Context Protocol (MCP) in velikih jezikovnih modelov. Razvit je bil prototip proizvodnega sistema, ki naravni jezik prevaja v operacije prek 35 orodij MCP. Na 175 testih sta bila primerjana oblačni model OpenAI in lokalni model Ollama glede točnosti, hitrosti, kakovosti in zvestobe odgovorov. Ugotovljeno je bilo, da lokalni model doseže primerljivo točnost pri rutinskih ukazih in enakovredno kakovost odgovora, a je približno šestnajstkrat počasnejši ter manj zanesljiv pri zahtevnih ukazih z več argumenti.

title: Biomimetic Phononic Channels for Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence: Non-Markovian Vibronic Coupling, Thermal-Fluctuation Harvesting, and Generalized Adaptive Phonon-Gates in Solid-State Qubit Architectures
abstract: Description / Abstract: A central dogma of modern quantum information science asserts that macroscopic quantum superposition in solid-state devices requires millikelvin cryogenic environments ($T \approx 10\text{--}15\,\text{mK}$) to freeze out thermal phononic decoherence. Conversely, natural biological complexes---such as the Fenna-Matthews-Olson (FMO) photosynthetic light-harvesting complex and avian cryptochrome magnetoreceptors---sustain functional electronic and spin quantum coherences at physiological temperatures ($T \approx 300\,\text{K}$). Biology resolves the thermal paradox not by suppressing environmental thermal fluctuations, but by employing structured, non-Markovian vibronic protein environments that actively harvest ambient heat to dynamically repump coherent phase trajectories. This treatise establishes the theoretical foundation and solid-state engineering architecture for Biomimetic Phononic Channels (BPCs) that replicate biological coherence mechanisms in artificial solid-state qubit platforms: (1) We formulate a non-Markovian open quantum Hamiltonian wherein engineered acoustic modes couple resonantly to electronic spin and transmon transitions, creating an underdamped vibronic shield with structured Lorentzian spectral densities; (2) We demonstrate the Environment-Assisted Quantum Transport (ENAQT) harvesting mechanism, proving that tuned non-Markovian phonon modes convert broadband thermal noise into constructive phase-locking drivers, attenuating the pure dephasing rate $\Gamma_\phi \to 0$ even as $k_B T \gg \hbar \omega_{\text{qubit}}$; and (3) We generalize our foundational Adaptive Phonon-Gate into the Generalized Adaptive Phonon-Gate (GAPG), utilizing piezoelectric lithium niobate ($\text{LiNbO}_3$) and diamond acoustic metamaterial superlattices to vent destructive incoherent high-frequency phonons while confining constructive vibronic modes. We present rigorous master equations, finite-element phononic bandgap dispersions, and benchmarking projections establishing a direct pathway toward room-temperature fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Developing salesperson AI wisdom along the B2B customer buying journey
abstract: AI in B2B sales is evolving beyond descriptive analytics toward prescriptive and generative tools that recommend, or even produce, a course of action. These outputs reach the salesperson looking like finished decisions, even though they often embed the priorities of whoever configured the tool, arrive too fast to examine, and remain invisible to the buyer. Foundational selling competencies were not built for this judgment. We introduce salesperson AI wisdom (SAIW), grounded in Sternberg’s Balance Theory of Wisdom, defined as the salesperson’s capability, developed through experience, to determine whether to follow, adapt, or override AI-generated outputs in ways that balance salesperson interests, buyer buying-job needs, and vendor organization objectives in pursuit of the common good. Anchored in the buyer’s journey, our framework maps SAIW across three stakeholder groups and six buying jobs from Jobs-to-Be-Done theory, positioning it as a moderator of how AI outputs translate into buyer-advancing actions. SAIW surfaces misalignment between the seller’s pipeline stage and the buyer’s current job that seller-centric models miss, distinguishes two wisdom enactment modes, and advances nine propositions on how it develops, moderates this translation, and is shaped by deployment mode, journey complexity, and vendor’s internal team actions.

title: A scoping review of transformer and large language model approaches for word sense disambiguation in multilingual and low resource settings from 2019 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Background In natural language processing, word sense disambiguation (WSD) is still a significant difficulty, especially in low-resource, multilingual environments with few annotated resources. Contextual semantic representation and WSD performance have been enhanced by recent developments in transformer architectures and large language models (LLMs). However, there is still little evidence synthesis in multilingual and genuine low-resource situations, and research is still dispersed across architectures, datasets, and evaluation systems. Methods In order to map evidence on transformer and LLM-based Word Sense Disambiguation techniques published between 2019 and January 2026, this scoping study used the PRISMA-ScR methodology. Google Scholar database was searched for relevant literatures. Studies that used transformer or LLM-based techniques for WSD and reported evaluation criteria like accuracy or F1-score were considered eligible. A structured framework comprising model architectures, datasets, evaluation techniques, adaption strategies, and important discoveries was used to chart the data descriptively. Results Nine studies were included in the analysis. Gloss-aware transformers, poly-encoder architectures, multilingual transfer learning, morphologically aware fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adapters, and LLM-based reasoning were among the main topics. Model scale alone does not seem to have as much of an impact on WSD performance as architectural design and contextual modeling. Evidence for really low-resource languages was still scarce, though. Conclusion Transformer and LLM-based methods show immense potential for improving WSD in multilingual contexts. However, there are still gaps in robustness assessment, benchmark standardization, and the wider inclusion of low-resource languages that are underrepresented.

title: Open-set encrypted traffic recognition via contrastively-optimized multi-modal gating and extreme value theory
abstract: The widespread adoption of cryptographic protocols has rendered traditional payload inspection ineffective, necessitating advanced encrypted traffic analysis. Identifying unseen zero-day threats within encrypted streams, defined as the open-set problem, remains challenging due to adversarial feature manipulation, metric distortion induced by traditional cross-entropy optimization, and the resulting overconfidence of closed-set classifiers. In this paper, we propose Contrastively-Optimized Multi-Modal Gating with Extreme Value Theory (COMG-EVT), an open-set encrypted traffic recognition framework designed to establish strict rejection boundaries for unknown attacks. The framework integrates three core mechanisms: a dynamic GatedFusion module that leverages stable microscopic payload entropy to modulate vulnerable macroscopic topological graphs, mitigating shortcut learning against obfuscation; a two-stage graph contrastive optimization paradigm that improves representation consistency and class-aware latent-space organization to reduce metric distortion; and a calibrated multi-gate EVT engine that models extreme tail distributions to mathematically bound the open space. We conduct extensive experiments on two contemporary datasets, including the cipher-agnostic CipherSpectrum dataset. The analytical results demonstrate that COMG-EVT outperforms state-of-the-art open-set methodologies, effectively minimizing the false positive rate for zero-day attacks while maintaining high classification accuracy for known traffic categories, thereby exhibiting robust resilience against dynamic open-space risks. Not applicable.

title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations
abstract: This paper studies Wong--Zakai convergence and Fourier neural operator learning for stochastic Volterra integral equations (SVIEs) describing random systems with memory. A Wong--Zakai theorem establishes convergence of pathwise solutions driven by piecewise linear approximations of Brownian motion to the corresponding SVIE solution. This convergence provides a foundation for using mirror-padded Fourier neural operators to learn the solution operator mapping initial conditions and driving noise to entire solution trajectories. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive prediction accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those used for training, while assessing the influence of padding and computational cost. As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.

title: Fairness under Prediction Error in Predict-then-Optimize Pipelines
abstract: Fairness constraints in predict-then-optimize pipelines are necessarily enforced on predicted outcomes $\hat{y}$, since true outcomes $y$ are unobserved at decision time. We study whether a demographic parity constraint enforced this way continues to hold against $y$, and how the resulting violation scales with prediction error. Using a budget-constrained allocation problem solved as a linear program, we show empirically that the true-outcome fairness gap grows with prediction error $σ$ and saturates, well fit by $c(1 - e^{-σ/τ})$ with $c = 0.1545 \pm 0.0103$ and $τ= 3.9045 \pm 0.3745$; its mean is invariant to sample size while its variance decays at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ rate. We derive a two-part theoretical bound: a closed-form local sensitivity result showing the gap's first-order response to prediction error depends on only two individuals per group, validated against the solver to within three significant figures; and a universal, error-independent ceiling following from the boundedness of the decision variable, confirmed consistent with but looser than the empirical saturation level. On US Census income data, enforcing demographic parity on a trained predictor's output reduces an unconstrained disparity in true income to roughly one-third of its original size, leaving 34.4% $\pm$ 3.3% (California) and 35.7% $\pm$ 1.8% (Texas) of the disparity intact and undetectable from the predictions alone -- consistent not only in mechanism but in approximate magnitude across two states with different demographics and income distributions, and stable across ten independent train/test splits in each. A fairness constraint that appears fully satisfied at decision time can mask a substantial, systematic violation of the outcome it was meant to protect.

title: FASHION-RQ: Mining Hierarchical Semantic Structure for Automated Evaluation of Fashion Retrieval
abstract: Evaluating fashion retrieval systems remains challenging due to the limited availability of benchmarks that capture the fine-grained, open-ended queries encountered in real-world search and recommendation. Existing benchmarks often rely on manual curation, predefined taxonomies, or synthetic prompts, limiting scalability and semantic coverage. We introduce FASHION-RQ: Mining Hierarchical Semantic Structure for Automated Evaluation of Fashion Retrieval, an automated framework that derives user-type queries and relevance sets directly from catalog structure. Our key insight is that hierarchical discrete representations learned by Residual Quantized Variational Autoencoders (RQ-VAE) organize products into semantically coherent clusters at progressively finer granularities. We leverage this structure to construct FASHION-RQBENCH, a scalable benchmark without manual query annotation or predefined taxonomies. We propose four complementary tasks for evaluating ranking, relevance classification, fine-grained sibling discrimination, and paraphrase robustness, alongside query- and attribute-level relevance metrics. Experiments across recent retrieval models demonstrate that FASHION-RQBENCH differentiates model capabilities across query types and attributes. A human study further shows that benchmark queries achieve comparable naturalness and higher intent clarity than real user queries, supporting their validity for real-world evaluation. The code and FASHION-RQBENCH dataset will be publicly released upon acceptance.

title: MemAct: Streaming Spatial Understanding with Memory and Active Exploration
abstract: Spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents navigating and interacting with the physical world. As observations arrive incrementally, agents must reason in a streaming manner. Yet streaming understanding must also be closed-loop: task-relevant evidence may require both recalling past observations and actively acquiring new views. Existing streaming approaches largely emphasize processing incoming observations, leaving task-driven active exploration underexplored. We introduce MemAct, a framework for streaming spatial understanding with memory and action. A shared vision--language model incrementally writes structured historical memory, retrieves records and past frames on demand, and acquires additional evidence through movement and turning. Retrieved evidence and action observations inform subsequent decisions, enabling the agent to continue exploring or answer within a unified reasoning loop. We develop the MemAct suite, a data generation pipeline and collection across real and simulated environments, with approximately 1M training examples for spatial reasoning, memory writing, retrieval, and exploration. Its MemAct-bench comprises 20,000 main QA pairs evaluating current-observation understanding, historical evidence use, and active exploration, plus 2,000 separate Timing questions. MemAct combines supervised fine-tuning for memory and interaction with counterfactual action optimization using cumulative evidence gains, action costs, and terminal answer quality to improve exploration and stopping decisions. Experiments show that MemAct outperforms existing spatial understanding and streaming baselines and approaches frontier multimodal models on MemAct-bench while retaining streaming inference efficiency.

title: Algorithms for evaluating and optimizing the quality of automatically generated questions from learning materials
abstract: V diplomskem delu je obravnavano vrednotenje kakovosti učnih vprašanj, ki jih iz učnih gradiv samodejno generirajo veliki jezikovni modeli. Zasnovan je hevristični ocenjevalni algoritem s štirimi uteženimi kriteriji, prilagojen slovenščini, in optimizacijska zanka, ki šibka vprašanja izboljšuje s ponovnim generiranjem ter razvrščanjem kandidatov. Sistem je zaokrožen v spletno aplikacijo. Na 989 vprašanjih dveh generatorjev so bile strojne ocene primerjane s človeško presojo in z jezikovnim modelom v vlogi sodnika. Pokazano je, da oba strojna ocenjevalca zgrešita večino vsebinsko slabih vprašanj, zato je predlagana večstopenjska arhitektura vrednotenja.

title: ANÁLISE COMPARATIVA DE SISTEMAS DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL APLICADOS À MAMOGRAFIA E SUAS CONTRIBUIÇÕES PARA A PRÁTICA BIOMÉDICA
abstract: A incorporação de tecnologias digitais e de recursos de inteligência artificial ao diagnóstico por imagem tem ampliado as possibilidades de suporte à avaliação mamográfica e à atuação dos profissionais da saúde. Nesse contexto, os sistemas de inteligência artificial voltados à análise e ao suporte diagnóstico apresentam diferentes funcionalidades e níveis de aplicabilidade, tornando necessária a compreensão de seus recursos e limitações. O presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar uma análise comparativa de sistemas de inteligência artificial relacionados ao diagnóstico por imagem, com ênfase na mamografia, buscando identificar suas principais funcionalidades e possíveis contribuições para a prática biomédica. Trata-se de um estudo exploratório, descritivo e comparativo, de abordagem predominantemente qualitativa, desenvolvido por meio de levantamento bibliográfico e análise documental. Foram consideradas informações provenientes de artigos científicos, fontes oficiais e documentação relacionada aos sistemas selecionados, sendo estabelecidos critérios para comparação quanto à finalidade, recursos tecnológicos, utilização de inteligência artificial, análise de imagens, aplicabilidade e suporte à prática profissional. A análise evidenciou diferenças entre as ferramentas quanto às funcionalidades disponibilizadas, formas de utilização e possibilidades de integração ao processo de avaliação mamográfica. Observou-se que esses recursos apresentam potencial como ferramentas complementares ao trabalho profissional, especialmente no suporte à análise de imagens e à organização do fluxo de trabalho, sem substituir a avaliação e a tomada de decisão do profissional habilitado. Conclui-se que o conhecimento sobre as características, potencialidades e limitações dessas tecnologias é relevante para sua utilização responsável e para o acompanhamento da evolução tecnológica na área de diagnóstico por imagem.

title: Are Humans Building the Second Engine of an AI Capability Explosion? - How Human-AI Research Forms, Transfers and Reconstructs the Conditions for Explosive Growth in Verified Scientific Output
abstract: An AI capability explosion could have two distinguishable sources: improvements in models and transformations in the conditions that make automated research possible. We propose that their interaction could accelerate AI’s capacity to produce further advances. Human researchers may help create usable problems, methods, standards of evidence and revisable decisions that convert an existing model into a more effective research system. If these conditions become reliably transferable and can themselves be reconstructed as new problems arise, automated research could expand without a corresponding initial gain in the underlying model. If that expansion then improves subsequent models and the ability to establish new research conditions, the two sources could reinforce one another. Human learning, judgment and responsibility belong within this process rather than being held fixed outside it. We distinguish model improvement, expansion of effective research capability and growth in validated scientific output, and separate the automation of research execution from the automation of enabling-condition formation. This is a hypothesis about a possible source of explosive growth, not a report of an observed explosion, a growth theorem or an experimental protocol.

title: Pre-registration: Paradee (arXiv 2610.06817) distilled 8M-parameter TTS quality claims, replication with released code
abstract: Pre-registration frozen on 2026-10-12 (git commit 3491730c of the AegisMind analysis tree), before the first run of the released code by the depositor. Deposited after the fact on 13 Oct 2026: the files are byte-identical to that commit; the time of the freeze is the commit date, not this deposit date. States the claim under test, protocol, decision rule and controls; no results are included. Part of a private replication-intake pipeline; verdicts, where any exist, are held until the authors have had a chance to respond. A later pre-registration deposited before its run: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23327505.

title: Checkpoints: compact GEC with FLAN-T5-small
abstract: Fine-tuned google/flan-t5-small (77M parameters) checkpoints for M. A. ElTaweel and N. Negied, Rethinking FLAN-T5 for Grammatical Error Correction: Controlled Baselines, Full-Budget Ablations and Two-Stage Transfer with Little Human Data (manuscript under review, 2026). Code, configurations, splits and system outputs: https://github.com/MemoXk/compact-gec-flan-t5 (archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23326147). Archive Model Paper final_stage2.zip Final system: stage 1 (cleaned C4-200M + 15% no-edit pairs), then stage 2 (W&I+LOCNESS A+B+C, holdout disjoint by source sentence) Tables 4–7 final_stage1.zip Stage 1 of the final system (synthetic data only) Table 4; Table 6 (“Ours, stage 1”) nogate_stage2.zip Two-stage model without no-edit pairs Table 4 (no-edit ablation) nogate_stage1.zip Stage 1 without no-edit pairs (cleaned C4-200M, seed 42) Table 4 (cleaning and no-edit ablations) Each archive is a Hugging Face transformers model directory (configuration, weights, tokenizer). SHA-256 checksums of the archives are in SHA256SUMS.txt. Usage from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("final_stage2") model = AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained("final_stage2") x = tok("Correct the grammar in this sentence: She go to school every days.", return_tensors="pt") y = model.generate(**x, num_beams=5, length_penalty=0.7, no_repeat_ngram_size=3, max_length=128) print(tok.decode(y[0], skip_special_tokens=True)) The paper’s full pipeline adds a guarded refinement pass and a confidence threshold (τ = 0); see notebooks/R2_D_stage2_dedup.ipynb in the code repository. Licence and intended use The weights are derived from google/flan-t5-small (Apache-2.0). The stage-2 checkpoints were trained on W&I+LOCNESS, which is licensed for non-commercial research and education only, so all four checkpoints are released under CC BY-NC 4.0, for non-commercial research use. The models make mistakes and can change the meaning of a sentence; do not use them for consequential decisions about learners.

title: Privacy-preserving techniques in visual computing: applications, challenges, and future directions
abstract: The proliferation of imaging technologies across healthcare, agriculture, environments, and consumer applications has heightened concerns regarding the privacy and security of visual data, which may contain biometric, medical, spatial, and location-specific information. Although federated learning (FL), differential privacy (DP), and secure multi-party computation (SMPC) have been reviewed as individual privacy-preserving approaches, existing surveys have predominantly examined these mechanisms in isolation from privacy-aware design principles. Moreover, limited attention has been given to imaging as a data modality, despite modality-specific privacy, and information leakage risks that differ from those associated with tabular and textual data. To address this research gap, this mini-review adopts a PRISMA-guided systematic review methodology to examine the literature on privacy-preserving approaches for imaging applications. An initial corpus of more than 5,000 records was screened and refined to a final set of 50 high-quality journal and conference publications based on publisher reliability, venue quality, and reporting rigor. The review establishes four dimensions of novelty in comparison with existing surveys and provides a characterization of five imaging sectors. For each sector, representative applications derived from implementations are examined alongside mathematically formalized challenges associated with federated learning, differential privacy, and secure multi-party computation. Trends in publication activity, application domains, and privacy-related challenges are analyzed through narrative and tabular presentations. Based on the synthesized evidence, the review contextualizes current adoption patterns and delineates prospective research directions for privacy-aware visual computing systems, distinguishing direct empirical observations from conceptual research trajectories.

title: Verification Turns Capability Gaps into Routing Decisions: Small Language Models for Clinical Documentation
abstract: Clinical note generation from doctor--patient dialogue is high-volume and hallucination-intolerant: a fabricated laboratory value can create patient-safety risk, not a quality regression. We ask whether an agentic \emph{verification} architecture, rather than generator scale, can make a small language model viable here. Holding a four-evaluator verification stack and refinement policy fixed and swapping only the generator between a 4B-parameter model with a QLoRA adapter and a frontier baseline, the small model reaches $0.984$ claim-level factual entailment against $0.992$ and comes within $3.3$ points on completeness, generating entirely on-device. Its deficit is confined to \emph{inter-section structural fidelity}---arrangement rather than clinical comprehension, and the axis on which it also falls furthest below the corpus's reference notes. Because that deficit is an explicit verifier decision rather than a silent quality difference, it becomes a routing policy: run the small model by default, escalate what the verifier rejects. Measured end to end, that it achieved a similiar verified-rate acceptance to the frontier-only acceptance in this test set ($99.6\%$ vs.\ $98.4\%$ over $250$ encounters) while routing $62$, documenting three quarters without a frontier \emph{generation} call. Ablating the loop separates architecture from scale: unrefined, the small model is accepted on $26.8\%$ of encounters and the frontier model on $74.8\%$, so verification does the most work where the generator is weakest. We also contribute section-scoped refinement, which preserves unflagged sections by construction rather than instruction, and find the baseline is not uniformly stronger---its provider refused two trauma-related transcripts the on-device model handled and certified, one facet of a provider dependency a served adapter does not carry.

title: Federated Unlearning of Quantum Data via Classical Shadows
abstract: Quantum federated learning trains a quantum neural network (QNN) across nodes that hold quantum data, such as the states of quantum sensors. To forget data, unlearning methods for quantum models replay them, and federated unlearning from stored updates removes whole nodes only. Quantum data cannot be replayed, since a state is consumed when measured and cannot be cloned. We propose Shadow-based Data Erasure (SHADE), in which each node records a classical shadow of every training state, a few randomized single-qubit measurements taken at training time. The gradient and curvature of a QNN on a state are expectations of observables, so SHADE estimates them for the forget data from the shadows at any later parameters and removes their effect by a federated Newton correction. Only classical estimates cross the network. We prove that the shadow size needed for a target unlearning error grows exponentially in the size of the backward light cone of the measured observable and not in the number of qubits. In simulation with 50 nodes and on edge boards, SHADE matches the forget accuracy of retraining within 0.5 points, without replay and in under 0.2 s.

title: Syntactic and Semantic Guidance for Automated Program Reasoning
abstract: In the past few years, the landscape of software development has been reshaped. Large Language Models have made generating code, proofs, tests, and documentation cheap and abundant. A generated artifact may look plausible yet be subtly wrong. At the pace generation now runs, manual review cannot close the gap. Generation is cheap; review is the bottleneck. This dissertation investigates how to establish formal guarantees for code at scale, with minimal human oversight. The first part of this dissertation studies mechanisms for enforcing strict syntactic constraints during LLM generation. In particular, we focus on Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD), which integrates formal grammar parsers directly into the decoding process. To make this approach practical for modern LLMs with large vocabularies, we develop techniques to improve the efficiency of grammar-aware decoding. We also identify a fundamental theoretical limitation of GCD: although it guarantees syntactic validity, it can distort the model’s learned probability distribution. To address this limitation, we introduce the Grammar-Aligned Decoding (GAD) problem, which seeks to align the sampling distribution with the desired structural constraints. While syntax can often be captured by explicit grammars, semantic correctness is substantially harder to specify. The second part of this dissertation addresses the problem of synthesizing precise semantic specifications from source code. We introduce a counterexample-guided synthesis algorithm that generates sound and precise program specifications within a target domain-specific language. We further extend this algorithm to nondeterministic programs, enabling the synthesis of both over-approximate and under-approximate specifications. The third part of this dissertation builds on these component-level specifications to synthesize complex systems compositionally. Rather than verifying or generating a large system monolithically, our approach constructs larger programs from existing sub-programs and verified lemmas. Each synthesis task is reduced to a smaller subproblem of the same general form, keeping the search space and proof obligations bounded at the component level. Together, these techniques provide a robust path toward the scalable, specification-guided construction of verified software systems.

title: A Hierarchical Option-Critic Soft Actor-Critic Framework for Adaptive Intelligent Control of Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Motion Systems
abstract: Multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) motion systems are widely employed in precision manufacturing, intelligent robotics, semiconductor equipment, and vision-guided automation, where coordinated control across multiple axes is essential for accurate and stable operation. However, inter-axis coupling, nonlinear dynamics, actuator interactions, and external disturbances pose significant challenges to achieving precise control under dynamically varying conditions. Conventional model-based and data-driven methods often depend on predefined system models or static state-to-action mappings, which can limit their adaptability to complex and changing motion behaviors. To address these challenges, this study develops a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, termed Option-Critic Soft Actor–Critic (OC-SAC), for adaptive continuous control of multi-DOF motion systems. The framework integrates the temporal abstraction of Option-Critic with the entropy-regularized continuous control of Soft Actor–Critic, enabling high-level option selection for long-horizon control strategies and low-level policy optimization for fine-grained motion adjustments. Double-Q learning and Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) are further incorporated to mitigate value overestimation and improve the utilization of informative experiences during off-policy learning. The proposed framework is evaluated using the Ant-v5 benchmark and a customized Gym-based multi-DOF error-state control environment. Experimental results show that OC-SAC provides improved convergence behavior and control performance compared with representative reinforcement learning algorithms, while maintaining effective error compensation in the customized multi-DOF environment. These results demonstrate the applicability of hierarchical reinforcement learning to adaptive control of complex multi-DOF motion systems under varying operating conditions.

title: Impact of Class Imbalance Correction on Biological Feature Selection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Methylation Data
abstract: Class imbalance is common in biomedical machine learning, yet imbalance-correction strategies are typically evaluated using predictive performance rather than their effects on biological interpretation. We evaluated six resampling methods: Random Oversampling (ROS), Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN), Random Undersampling (RUS), ClusterCentroids, and AllKNN (All K-Nearest Neighbors), together with a no-resampling baseline, using DNA methylation data from The Cancer Genome Atlas Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cohort. The analysis included 485,578 CpG markers of which 406,807 were retained after quality-control filtering. A continuous feature-ranking framework merging Random Forest importance and ANOVA F-statistics was applied across repeated runs. Biological relevance was evaluated through hypergeometric enrichment against a curated PDAC gene set and preranked Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) using 309 Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways. All seven analysis strategies produced significant enrichment for literature-supported pancreatic cancer-associated genes, with hypergeometric p-values ranging from 3.34×10−16 to 1.28×10−7. SMOTE recovered the largest absolute number of PDAC-associated genes (141 of 13,827 selected genes), whereas RUS achieved the greatest fold enrichment (2.17-fold; 88 observed versus 40.61 expected). Notably, the no-resampling baseline remained highly competitive, recovering 112 PDAC-associated genes with 1.86-fold enrichment and a p-value of 5.27×10−14, indicating that resampling was not necessary to recover biologically relevant features under the evaluated feature-ranking framework. Across methods, 169–234 of the 309 tested KEGG pathways were significant at false discovery rate ≤0.05. ClusterCentroids produced the largest number of significant pathways (234), followed by the no-resampling baseline (225) and RUS (223). evidence.title: Impact of Class Imbalance Correction on Biological Feature Selection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Methylation Data
evidence.abstract: Class imbalance is common in biomedical machine learning, yet imbalance-correction strategies are typically evaluated using predictive performance rather than their effects on biological interpretation. title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
abstract: Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. Classical approaches, such as Sequential Monte Carlo ABC, rely on handcrafted summary statistics and scale poorly across large parameter spaces. To overcome this, we introduce a neural inference architecture. Our pipeline utilizes shared 1D-CNNs and a permutation-invariant Set Attention mechanism to learn low-dimensional summary statistics from variable-length, multi-experiment time-series data. These statistics simultaneously condition a model selection network to compute posterior model probabilities and model-specific conditional Invertible Neural Networks (cINNs) that estimate parameter posterior distributions. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.

title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.

title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
abstract: Generating information-rich visual artifacts such as slides, posters, and dashboards as code is appealing because the outputs are structured, editable, and verifiable. Yet code models cannot see how their choices of layout and color come together on the canvas, often limiting spatial planning and aesthetic quality. Image generators excel at visual design but can misrender requested content, making their outputs unreliable targets for direct reproduction. We therefore introduce AesCode, which generates code grounded in the content prompt while using an image generated from the same prompt as an aesthetic guidance. To do so, AesCode represents the target as a design graph that describes the whole canvas and makes each property attributable. From this graph, we derive complementary cross-modal rewards: deterministic verifiers score properties parsable from code and rendering, while a VLM judge assesses the non-parsable ones with a sample-specific Visual Graph Rubric (VGR) tied to graph elements and relations. We optimize these decoupled rewards through reinforcement learning with per-channel normalization to jointly improve spatial planning, aesthetic quality, and verifiable correctness. To evaluate this setting, we build a benchmark that scores verifiable correctness and visual quality separately, with visual scores highly consistent with human judgments. We find that reference images substantially improve the visual quality of code generated by existing models, and ablations show that AesCode benefits from references both as model input and as a source of visual rewards. Relative to same-scale Qwen3-VL baselines given the same references, AesCode-8B and AesCode-32B improve visual quality by 31.1 and 22.4 percentage points, reaching scores comparable to those of closed-source frontier models such as GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8.

title: Dynamic K-Head: Difficulty-Supervised Budget Selection for Continuous Latent Reasoning
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) improves reasoning but incurs substantial autoregressive rationale cost. Continuous CoT moves intermediate computation into recurrent hidden states, yet typically uses a fixed number of updates even though the best budget varies across questions and accuracy need not improve monotonically with $K$. We introduce Dynamic K-Head, a question-conditioned, pre-rollout budget selector. It is jointly trained with the reasoner under selected budgets, using difficulty supervision based on scores assigned from the question alone. We also show that latent-update count can misrepresent end-to-end cost because a short latent rollout can shift computation into a longer explicit continuation. We therefore count latent updates, implementation-specific special tokens, and all decoded text. Instantiated with CoDI on Llama 3.2 1B and GSM8K, Dynamic K-Head reaches 54.44% exact-match accuracy at 12.03 average reasoning/output tokens, compared with 52.31% at 15.21 tokens for fixed-$K=6$ CoDI---a 2.12-point gain with 20.9% lower token cost. Across three out-of-distribution arithmetic datasets, it reduces cost by 19.3--25.7% while improving accuracy by 0.30--2.22 points. These results demonstrate that difficulty-supervised budget selection can improve both accuracy and efficiency, while stable budget selection remains a central challenge.

title: THE BUSINESS POTENTIAL OF QUANTUM TECHNOLOGIES
abstract: Kvantne tehnologije temeljijo na zakonih fizike, ki jih raziskuje znanstvena veda pod imenom kvantna mehanika. Za svoje delovanje izkoriščajo kvantne učinke za zbiranje, obdelavo in prenos informacij. Ne gre za nekaj novega, saj so se začele uporabljati že z jedrsko energijo in postavile temelje za polprevodnike, ki omogočajo delovanja današnjih pametnih telefonov. Na podlagi razumevanja delovanja posameznih delcev se v zadnjem obdobju na področju kvantnih tehnologij dogajajo prelomne novosti. Kvantne tehnologije so širši pojem, ki zajemajo ožja področja, kot so kvantna senzorika, kvantno računalništvo in kvantna komunikacija. V praksi se posamezne kvantne tehnologije pogosto zelo prepletajo. Ob omembi besede »kvantno« danes najprej pomislimo na kvantno računalništvo. Čeprav kvantno računalništvo res pritegne največ pozornosti in naložb, se pomembne raziskave izvajajo tudi na področju kvantne senzorike in kvantne komunikacije. Kvantna senzorika omogoča izredno natančne meritve z veliko občutljivostjo. Kvantna komunikacija omogoča varen prenos informacij. Kvantno računalništvo pa bo reševalo probleme, ki so prezahtevni za danes najboljše klasične računalnike in superračunalnike. Že na samem začetku ugotovimo, da gre pri kvantnih tehnologijah za popolnoma nov pogled. Kvantno računalništvo pa ni le hitrejša različica klasičnega računalništva, temveč gre za popolnoma drugačno napravo, ki zahteva drugačen pristop in ponudi drugačen način reševanja najbolj kompleksnih problemov. Kot da bi rekli, da je žarnica le zmogljivejša oblika sveče. Predstavili smo različne potenciale kvantnih tehnologij v različnih gospodarskih sektorjih s praktičnimi primeri ter orisali predvideno smer raziskav in razvoja kvantnih tehnologij. Dotaknili smo se zasebnih in javnih investicij ter geopolitičnega pomena kvantnih tehnologij.

title: EL-RAKHAWI ARCHITECTURE FOR TOPOLOGICAL PHOTONIC NEUROMORPHIC COMPUTING WITH NEAR-ZERO THERMAL DISSIPATION
abstract: TPNC-NZTD: TOPOLOGICAL PHOTONIC NEUROMORPHIC COMPUTING WITH NEAR-ZERO THERMAL DISSIPATION Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-RakhawiDOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23337933 A revolutionary hybrid chip architecture solving AI's energy crisis by integrating three Nobel Prize-winning phenomena: photonic computing (light instead of electrons), topological insulators (backscattering-immune edge states), and spiking neural networks (event-driven computation). Core architecture: 2D topological insulator substrate (bismuthene on SiC) + nanoscale photonic waveguides along edges + non-linear optical synapses (phase-change materials GeSbTe or 2D TMDs) + photonic neurons with thresholding behavior. Quantum-limited performance: Energy per photon at 1550 nm = 0.128 aJ. With 10-100 photons per spike for reliable detection above noise floor: E_spike = 10-100 aJ (100-1000× improvement over electronic SNNs). Thermal dissipation: 10 aJ × 1 MHz × 10⁶ synapses = 10 μW per million synapses (1,000,000× improvement over electronic chips). Computational speed: 100 GHz - 1 THz via photonic propagation. Fabrication: CMOS BEOL-compatible via heterogeneous integration (micro-transfer printing or adhesive wafer bonding of III-V materials), preserving topological bandgap integrity during processing. Applications: Edge AI/IoT ($50B), data center acceleration ($150B), autonomous systems ($30B), scientific computing ($20B), neuromorphic research ($5B). Total addressable market: $300B+ by 2030. Comprehensive IP protection: 5 patent claims covering hybrid architecture, photonic spike computation method, heterogeneous fabrication process preserving topological states, synaptic weight update protocols, and application-specific deployments. Trade secrets, perpetual moral rights under Berne Convention, 4 protected trademarks. All rights reserved, proprietary. Full citation: El-Rakhawi, M. K. A. (2026). El-Rakhawi Architecture for Topological Photonic Neuromorphic Computing with Near-Zero Thermal Dissipation (TPNC-NZTD). Ismailia, Egypt. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23337933.
