title: Chordal Codes: Code Construction and Efficient Gaussian-Elimination Decoding
abstract: Maximum-likelihood decoding of linear codes over erasure channels can be considered as solving a linear system of a column submatrix of the parity-check matrix. In practice, Gaussian elimination is usually applied, and its computational cost depends on the structure of the matrix, especially the sparsity and the fill-in generated during the elimination. The \emph{chordal graph}, or \emph{triangulated graph}, first introduced by C. Berge, has a so-called \emph{perfect elimination ordering}, indicating that if the primal graph of a matrix is a chordal graph, then there exists a perfect elimination ordering such that a special class of fill-in under Gaussian elimination following this ordering will be avoided. In this paper, we introduce \emph{chordal codes}, i.e., codes equipped with parity-check matrices such that the primal graphs of the parity-check matrices are chordal. We prove that, for a chordal code, the decoding submatrix associated with any erasure pattern retains a chordal primal graph. So, the complexity of chordal elimination (Gaussian elimination following the perfect elimination ordering applied to the chordal code decoding) will be smaller than decoding a random code by Gaussian elimination. Also, we provide an upper bound on the complexity of chordal elimination.

title: 重要語マスクに対する事前学習済みNLIモデルの反応
abstract: 【背景とハルシネーションへの位置づけ】近年、生成AI(大規模言語モデル)が事実に基づかない誤った情報を出力するハルシネーション(幻覚)の抑制は、実務上および研究上の最重要課題となっています。ハルシネーションを検出・修正するアプローチ(RARR や SelfCheckGPT など)では、生成された記述が「提示された根拠(外部知識)に真に依存しているか」を検証するプロセスが不可欠です。元の「MaskVerify草稿」は、根拠文内の重要語をマスク(隠蔽)した際のNLI(自然言語推論)モデルの判定変化を利用し、根拠に依存しない「見かけの支持(AIが内部知識やバイアスだけで尤もらしく同意してしまう現象)」を検出できると主張していました。これが実現すれば、ハルシネーションの自動検知やフィルタリングに直結します。【本稿におけるハルシネーションへの言及と限定的結論】しかしながら、実データ(SciFact)を用いた本探索的追試の結果、以下の通りハルシネーション対策への直接的な貢献については慎重な(限定的な)結論に至っています。• 直接的な測定の不在: 本試行では生成AI(LLM)による回答生成やハルシネーション発生率そのものは測定しておらず、金標準の根拠文に対する固定NLIモデルの語彙感度を測ったにとどまります。• 「見かけの支持」の識別困難: 重要語のマスクによって支持確率が大きく低下する(平均差 0.183)という「語彙重複への感応性」は観察されました。しかし、マスク後も支持判定が維持された例(18.6%)において、それが「AIの内部知識(ハルシネーションに繋がりうるバイアス)」によるものか、単に「マスク外の残存根拠」によるものかは現行データから識別できません。• 結論: したがって、本操作(語彙重複マスク)の感度差の数値だけで、直ちに「生成AIのハルシネーションを検出・低減できる信頼性の高い技術」と呼ぶことは時期尚早であり、さらなる検証(意味や文法を統制した対照実験など)が必要です。

title: A reason with the switch: what an agent memory pipeline passes on when fallback runs come with a stated purpose. Protocol and materials frozen before the run (Paper 7, Study 2; second registration)
abstract: Frozen protocol, code and materials of the second study of a paper on what LLM agents' memory-writing pipelines keep from a run of tool outcomes, deposited before any smoke or confirmatory model call under this registration (the manifest's OpenTimestamps proof is included; its Bitcoin attestation is checked by the gated launcher; the smoke of an earlier registration of this study ran before it, as described below). The first study (frozen and deposited as doi:10.5281/zenodo.23291437) found, descriptively, that after nine successes of a standard route and two runs on a fallback that the scripted agent made without a stated reason, almost every session reading the summaries of a replay of the memory pipeline of OpenAI's open-source Codex agent (default v1 instructions, pinned at commit ecebd679; an adapted replay, not the shipped pipeline) chose the fallback for the next run. This study gives the two fallback runs a reason in their requests (none; a bare request for the fallback; a dated check of the fallback set on the calendar before the runs; a permanent move to it), on the first study's 96 streams, and compares what fresh sessions reading the replay's summaries, a run log carrying the requests, or a record of per-route counts choose and forecast for the next run. The registered contrasts set the bare request against the dated check under the v1 summaries, the v1 summaries against the log under the check, and the two changes against each other; no choice is scored. This is the study's second registration (v1.1). The first (v1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23335172) ended at its smoke run, before any confirmatory call: the smoke could not meet its registered criteria (18 of one reader's 30 requests ended without an answer, 15 in a provider's outage and 3 refused as rate-limited after it; and the rule for invalid answers, taken from the first study's larger smoke, allowed a reader one invalid answer among its 30 requests, which two refusals of another reader exceeded). Section 13 of the registration reports that attempt. This registration differs from the first in the smoke's criteria (refusals are counted apart; four criteria are added) and in nothing that concerns the design, the cells, the contrasts or the analysis. The archive holds the registration (REGISTRATION.md), the design memos, the study's code, which runs the first study's frozen files, unchanged in their bytes, on the new tree (replacing some of their functions as they are loaded, as the registration states), every file of the first study that it executes or reads (byte-identical to the first study's freeze manifest, which the code checks at import), the request notes and the codebook of the two model coders, the coder pilot's gates and summary, the power, size and spend tables, the wave-1 writer schedule, the pre-freeze reviews of the design and of the package with their dispositions, and the chain scripts. MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file with its SHA-256; MANIFEST.sha256.ots is its OpenTimestamps proof. Manifest SHA-256: 1bceeed0bcb50ce1cc4057f5ddb4175499fc3026a16bc84deca06735c9910731. Zip SHA-256: 91408e7033fb5fcf1e4dd3a7e0205e8bc649cbc997e1d16d4954bf86a9290b46. No result of this study is included. Licences: paper7/study2/LICENSE.md and, for the first study's files, paper7/study1/LICENSE.md.

title: Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data Generation via Differential Privacy and Generative AI: Architectures, Utility Bounds, and Attack Verification
abstract: Abstract—The cross-organizational sharing of high-dimensional empirical datasets—such as electronic health records, financial credit transactions, and telecommunications telemetry—is fundamentally constrained by strict data governance legislation (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA). Heuristic sanitization methods (such as k-anonymity, l-diversity, and pseudo-anonymization) have repeatedly proven vulnerable to linkage and re-identification attacks. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)—encompassing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs)—offers the capability to synthesize structurally authentic surrogate populations. However, unconstrained generative models memorize sensitive training instances within their parameter weights, exposing downstream deployments to Membership Inference Attacks (MIA) and Attribute Disclosure Attacks. Differential Privacy (DP) provides the mathematical standard to guarantee bounded information leakage independent of adversarial prior knowledge. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data Generation uniting Generative AI with Differential Privacy. We formalize the Renyi Differential Privacy (RDP) accounting framework, model gradient perturbation dynamics under Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD), and evaluate discrete marginal mechanisms (PrivBayes, PGM) alongside continuous generative models (DP-WGAN, DP-Diffusion). Furthermore, we construct an enterprise benchmarking testbed across three high-dimensional, sensitive datasets (MIMIC-III clinical records, German Credit, and Census PUMS). Our findings demonstrate that while unconstrained generative synthesis suffers a 74.2% membership inference vulnerability, DP-Diffusion governed by (epsilon = 1.0, delta = 10^-5) bounds attacker advantage to near-random guessing (51.8%) while preserving 91.4% downstream machine learning classification utility. Finally, we formulate open challenges in high-dimensional privacy budgeting, multi-modal alignment, and verified auditing frameworks. Index Terms—Differential Privacy (DP), Generative AI, Synthetic Data Generation, DP-SGD, Diffusion Models, Membership Inference Attacks (MIA), Renyi Differential Privacy, Data Governance.

However, unconstrained generative models memorize sensitive training instances within their parameter weights, exposing downstream deployments to Membership Inference Attacks (MIA) and Attribute Disclosure Attacks. Differential Privacy (DP) provides the mathematical standard to guarantee bounded information leakage independent of adversarial prior knowledge. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data Generation uniting Generative AI with Differential Privacy. We formalize the Renyi Differential Privacy (RDP) accounting framework, model gradient perturbation dynamics under Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD), and evaluate discrete marginal mechanisms (PrivBayes, PGM) alongside continuous generative models (DP-WGAN, DP-Diffusion). Furthermore, we construct an enterprise benchmarking testbed across three high-dimensional, sensitive datasets (MIMIC-III clinical records, German Credit, and Census PUMS). Our findings demonstrate that while unconstrained generative synthesis suffers a 74.2% membership inference vulnerability, DP-Diffusion governed by (epsilon = 1.0, delta = 10^-5) bounds attacker advantage to near-random guessing (51.8%) while preserving 91.4% downstream machine learning classification utility. Finally, we formulate open challenges in high-dimensional privacy budgeting, multi-modal alignment, and verified auditing frameworks. Index Terms—Differential Privacy (DP), Generative AI, Synthetic Data Generation, DP-SGD, Diffusion Models, Membership Inference Attacks (MIA), Renyi Differential Privacy, Data Governance.

title: Verifiable Blind Pseudonymization via Polymorphic Encryption Using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
abstract: Pseudonymization is a basic technique for privacy protection, limiting identifiability and linkability of data. Data can be pseudonymized blindly, i.e., while being end-to-end encrypted, using the Polymorphic Encryption and Pseudonymization (PEP) framework. This means that the party performing pseudonymization does not see the values of pseudonyms and cannot determine if two (encrypted) pseudonyms belong to each other, ensuring confidentiality and unlinkability. The pseudonymizing party can, however, unnoticeably corrupt any data being exchanged. This violates integrity. We present an extension of the PEP framework that does guarantee integrity without breaking its unlinkability features. With this, we bring the verifiability technique of two-party verifiable oblivious pseudorandom functions (OPRFs, RFC 9497) to the more advanced three-party setting of PEP. Where related systems use bilinear pairings to verify plaintext pseudonyms, our approach proves correct transformation of ciphertexts using Schnorr-style non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs that require no pairings and run on standard, fast curves such as Curve25519, making it significantly more efficient and practical to implement while offering similar privacy guarantees. We also show that the interplay between verifiability and unlinkability requires careful analysis: making rerandomization verifiable defeats the unlinkability it provides, and preserving pseudonym confidentiality requires reshuffling and rekeying to be proved jointly while rerandomization is proved separately.

title: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation With Stage-Wise Shared Adapters
abstract: Different MRI modalities reveal different parts of a brain tumor. Segmentation models combine information from these modalities to outline tumor regions. Many models use a separate encoder for each modality. However, exchanging features among these encoders at several stages can increase model complexity. We introduce the Block-Wise Shared Adapter (BWSA), which combines compressed features from the modality encoders in a shared path and returns adapted features to each stream. In its fixed-blending form, BWSA adds the adapted features to the original features. Its trainable-gated variant (TG-BWSA) instead learns separate weights for the original and adapted features at each modality and encoder stage. We evaluate both variants on BraTS 2020 and BraTS 2023 with four segmentation backbones. On the official BraTS 2023 online validation set, BWSA increases average region-wise Dice by 1.3--7.6 percentage points relative to the corresponding unmodified backbones. TG-BWSA increases it by 2.8--7.7 points. Both variants add approximately 0.85--3.73% parameters and reduce average HD95 relative to the unmodified backbones.

title: ShoeFit: A New Dataset and Dual-image-stream DiT Framework for Virtual Footwear Try-On
abstract: Virtual footwear try-on (VFTON), a critical yet underexplored area in virtual try-on (VTON), aims to synthesize faithful try-on results given diverse footwear and model images while maintaining 3D consistency and texture authenticity. Unlike conventional garment-focused VTON methods, VFTON presents unique challenges due to (1) Data Scarcity, which arises from the difficulty of perfectly matching product shoes with models wearing the identical ones, (2) Viewpoint Misalignment, where the target foot pose and source shoe views are always misaligned, leading to incomplete texture information and detail distortion, and (3) Background-induced Color Distortion, where complex material of footwear interacts with environmental lighting, causing unintended color contamination. To address these challenges, we introduce MVShoes, a multi-view shoe try-on dataset consisting of 7305 well-annotated image triplets, covering diverse footwear categories and challenging try-on scenarios. Furthermore, we propose a dual-stream DiT architecture, ShoeFit, designed to mitigate viewpoint misalignment through Multi-View Conditioning with 3D Rotary Position Embedding, and alleviate background-induced distortion using the LayeredRefAttention which leverages background features to modulate footwear latents. The proposed framework effectively decouples shoe appearance from environmental interferences while preserving high-quality texture detail through decoupled denoising and conditioning branches. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our method substantially improves rendering fidelity and robustness under challenging real-world product shoes, establishing a new benchmark in high-fidelity footwear try-on synthesis.

title: Follow the Perturbed Leader for Linear Bandits: $\sqrt{T}$ Regret over General Convex Sets
abstract: We give the first adversarial linear bandit algorithm based on Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) that achieves $\sqrt{T}$ regret over general convex action sets. Our algorithm attains $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^{5/4}\sqrt{T})$ regret using only linear optimization oracles, and the near-optimal $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d\sqrt{T})$ regret when an optimal-design exploration distribution is further available. This improves on the $T^{2/3}$ regret of the FTPL algorithm of Dani and Hayes (2006) for general convex sets, and generalizes the $\sqrt{T}$ regret of Lévy et al. (2026) over two special action sets (hypercube and Euclidean ball). Compared to previous oracle-efficient linear bandit algorithms based on continuous exponential weights, the FTPL approach generally has better computational efficiency, and is much simpler to implement. The key algorithmic element is a perturbation distribution that adapts to the past reward estimators. Its simplest form, an adaptive Gaussian perturbation, is straightforward to implement and already attains the regret bound above. We further extend it to two general constructions, random-weighting and elliptical perturbations, each covering distributions from light tails (Gaussian) to heavy tails (Student-$t_2$). On the technical side, we develop a systematic way to analyze the stability term in the FTPL regret through the Fisher information of the perturbation distribution. This builds a general framework for FTPL beyond existing ones such as the hazard rate and the FTRL-FTPL duality.

title: Python for Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences introduces programming from the perspective of a pharmacy student rather than a computer-science specialist. Concepts are developed progressively using pharmaceutical examples such as dose calculations, concentration conversions, assay data, dissolution profiles, calibration curves, pharmacokinetic datasets, stability studies and experimental data analysis.

title: Data and code for "Beyond Generation: What a Decision-Native Model Does Well in a Long Task, and What It Needs from Its Harness"
abstract: Data and code archive for the preprint Beyond Generation: What a Decision-Native Model Does Well in a Long Task, and What It Needs from Its Harness (Xuanming Cao, 2026). It contains every recorded run, request and response behind the paper (hidden reasoning redacted), the engine, controllers and analysis code, the protocols with dated amendments of three studies, and the manuscript source. No API credentials are included. paper/: manuscript source, figures, CLAIMS.md (each claim with its source), analysis scripts and outputs artifact/study/, study-v3/, study-v4/: Studies 1-3 (protocols, raw runs and calls, derived tables, schedules) artifact/vault/: engine, environment generator, controllers, adapters, tools; vault-study1-code-0c87abc/: the code that produced Study 1 artifact/demos/, artifact/history/: demonstrations and superseded drafts SHA256SUMS, PACKAGE-MANIFEST.json: per-file checksums Reproduce the numbers of the paper without network access: see README.md inside the archive. Code: MIT; data: CC BY 4.0. How to get the archive. Because uploads of large files kept failing, jev-study-v1.0.zip (147 MB) is stored as 47 pieces of 3 MiB named jev-study-v1.0.zip.001 … .047. Download all of them and run cat jev-study-v1.0.zip.0* > jev-study-v1.0.zip, check its SHA-256 (given in READ-ME-FIRST.txt), unzip, and start with jev-study-v1.0/README.md.

title: Datasets for paper "Discovering Encrypted Client Hello Deployments by Active ECH Probing"
abstract: This data is supplement to https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22012700 and contains the necessary data to recreate plots and tables of the following paper: Jonas Mücke, Konstantin Gasser, Thomas C. Schmidt, and Matthias Wählisch. 2026. Discovering Encrypted Client Hello Deployments by Active ECH Probing. In Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC '26). Association for Computing Machinery, New York, NY, USA, 276–286. https://doi.org/10.1145/3777912.3839832 Paper abstract: We present a new measurement method to detect ECH deployments. This method leverages standard-compliant behavior of ECH servers. Prior measurements relied on DNS exposure and reported only one major ECH deployment (Cloudflare). Our measurements reveal yet undiscovered ECH deployments, including a large deployment at Meta. Meta servers support ECH, but ECH configuration is not exposed via the DNS. We also empirically study details such as the level of privacy improvement and latency impact of ECH.

title: Методологічний підхід до виявлення патологічних змін на мамограмах із використанням вейвлет-аналізу
abstract: Раннє виявлення патологічних змін молочної залози є важливим завданням медичної діагностики, оскільки на початкових етапах захворювання патологічні структури можуть мати низький локальний контраст, невеликі розміри та маскуватися неоднорідною анатомічною структурою тканин.Це зумовлює актуальність розроблення методів автоматизованого аналізу цифрових мамографічних зображень, здатних враховувати просторові та багатомасштабні характеристики патологічних областей.У роботі запропоновано методологічний підхід до автоматизованого виявлення та локалізації патологічних змін на цифрових мамограмах на основі двовимірного дискретного вейвлет-перетворення. Сформовано відтворюваний алгоритм із фіксованими параметрами та оригінальним правилом формування карти підозрілості.Алгоритм передбачає сегментацію області молочної залози, анізотропну дифузію Перона-Маліка, локальне контрастування з використанням методу адаптивного вирівнювання гістограми з обмеженням контрасту, три-рівневу декомпозицію, м'яке порогування коефіцієнтів за універсальним порогом та обчислення локальних статистичних і текстурних характеристик.Наукову новизну становить критерій міжмасштабної узгодженості, за яким локальна підозрілість формується не лише з величини окремого вейвлет-коефіцієнта, а з узгодженості енергетичної, статистичної та просторовотекстурної характеристик на суміжних масштабах.Для різних типів мамографічних проявів задано окремі правила: мікрокальцинати аналізуються переважно за високочастотною енергією та ексцесом, маси -за низькочастотною структурою й текстурою, а структурні деформації -за міжнапрямною та міжмасштабною неоднорідністю.Визначено локальні вікна, фіксовані ваги компонентів карти та правила постобробки.Сформована методологія має модульну структуру, що забезпечує можливість окремого налаштування та подальшого вдосконалення її компонентів.Вона створює основу для програмної реалізації системи автоматизованого аналізу мамограм, результатом роботи якої може бути локалізований набір кандидатних областей із відповідними характеристиками.Практичним результатом подальшого розвитку методології є створення програмного модуля автоматизованого аналізу мамограм.Такий модуль може виконувати попередню обробку зображення, багатомасштабну вейвлет-декомпозицію, автоматичне формування карт підозрілості та виділення кандидатних областей.Результатом його роботи може бути не встановлення діагнозу, а структурований набір локалізованих областей із відповідними характеристиками, який використовується як додаткова інформація під час подальшої інтерпретації зображення спеціалістом.Подальші дослідження передбачають реалізацію алгоритму на відкритих анотованих наборах мамограм, окрему перевірку трьох типів патологічних проявів, аналіз чутливості до типу вейвлета та рівня декомпозиції.Подальше розширення методології може здійснюватися у напрямі машинного та глибокого навчання.Вейвлет-ознаки можуть використовуватися як вхідний простір для класичних алгоритмів класифікації, а сформовані карти підозрілості -як механізм попереднього визначення регіонів інтересу для згорткових нейронних мереж або інших моделей глибокого навчання.Перспективним є також дослідження гібридних архітектур, у яких багатомасштабне вейвлетпредставлення поєднується з автоматично навченими ознаками.У такій постановці запропонована методологія може виконувати функцію інтерпретованого та параметризованого етапу попереднього аналізу, доповнюючи можливості сучасних моделей машинного навчання.

окремого вейвлет-коефіцієнта, а з узгодженості енергетичної, статистичної та просторовотекстурної характеристик на суміжних масштабах.Для різних типів мамографічних проявів задано окремі правила: мікрокальцинати аналізуються переважно за високочастотною енергією та ексцесом, маси -за низькочастотною структурою й текстурою, а структурні деформації -за міжнапрямною та міжмасштабною неоднорідністю.Визначено локальні вікна, фіксовані ваги компонентів карти та правила постобробки.Сформована методологія має модульну структуру, що забезпечує можливість окремого налаштування та подальшого вдосконалення її компонентів.Вона створює основу для програмної реалізації системи автоматизованого аналізу мамограм, результатом роботи якої може бути локалізований набір кандидатних областей із відповідними характеристиками.Практичним результатом подальшого розвитку методології є створення програмного модуля автоматизованого аналізу мамограм.Такий модуль може виконувати попередню обробку зображення, багатомасштабну вейвлет-декомпозицію, автоматичне формування карт підозрілості та виділення кандидатних областей.Результатом його роботи може бути не встановлення діагнозу, а структурований набір локалізованих областей із відповідними характеристиками, який використовується як додаткова інформація під час подальшої інтерпретації зображення спеціалістом.Подальші дослідження передбачають реалізацію алгоритму на відкритих анотованих наборах мамограм, окрему перевірку трьох типів патологічних проявів, аналіз чутливості до типу вейвлета та рівня декомпозиції.Подальше розширення методології може здійснюватися у напрямі машинного та глибокого навчання.Вейвлет-ознаки можуть використовуватися як вхідний простір для класичних алгоритмів класифікації, а сформовані карти підозрілості -як механізм попереднього визначення регіонів інтересу для згорткових нейронних мереж або інших моделей глибокого навчання.Перспективним є також дослідження гібридних архітектур, у яких багатомасштабне вейвлетпредставлення поєднується з автоматично навченими ознаками.У такій постановці запропонована методологія може виконувати функцію інтерпретованого та параметризованого етапу попереднього аналізу, доповнюючи можливості сучасних моделей машинного навчання.

title: Recognition of Cognitive Intervention Effects and Modeling of Learning Behavior Patterns in Second Language Acquisition Using a Multimodal Intervention-Aware Temporal Graph Network
abstract: To distinguish between “text improvement” and “cognitive gain” in generative-AI-assisted second language learning, this study proposes a Multimodal Intervention-Aware Temporal Graph Network (MITG-Net). The method integrates human-AI dialogue, revision trajectories, behavioral logs, and learner attributes. Through intervention-conditioned dynamic weighting and heterogeneous temporal graph modeling, it captures the relationships among prompts, feedback, revisions, and transfer, and jointly performs intervention-effect recognition and learning-behavior-pattern discovery. Experiments were conducted on 744 learning sessions collected from 186 undergraduates at three universities. MITG-Net achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.816 and a weighted Kappa of 0.854, outperforming the strongest baseline, HGT, by 3.4 percentage points in Macro-F1. Removing behavioral logs and revision trajectories reduced Macro-F1 by 0.054 and 0.045, respectively. The model identified five behavior patterns. Among them, the strategy-transfer application pattern achieved an average effect level of 2.78 and a transfer score of 0.82, substantially higher than the 1.36 and 0.31 obtained by the AI-dominated direct-adoption pattern. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively recognize cognitive intervention effects and provide interpretable evidence for personalized support in second language learning.

title: Towards Training and Inference of Graph Neural Networks in Graph Databases
abstract: Graph Neural Networks on large graphs commonly rely on in-memory graph storage with ad hoc data processing pipelines for both training and inference. Graph databases provide scalable storage and efficient traversal for graphs that can evolve over time, but their applicability in GNN training and inference are rarely studied. We show that graph DBs can be used in GNN training and inference directly, executing sampling, feature retrieval, and even the full forward pass. We show different GNN training pipelines can perform on-the-fly sampling and retrieval in graph DBs using Cypher. We further provide optimisations that speed up the training process by \~2.5x while maintaining the same accuracy. We illustrate that fully in-DB inference is possible, independent of how the GNNs are trained. Our inference setup can be >10x faster than cold loading the graph into RAM with no extra memory overhead on real-world graphs. Our work lays the foundation for in-graph-DB GNN training and inference.

title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. Our 3D foundation model, anatomix, is used to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes, and we further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system won first place in the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at http://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.

title: Explicitly correlated ground states with a feedback-free variational hybrid algorithm
abstract: Explicitly correlated methods, which represent dominant short-range correlations by a diagonal Jastrow-type correlator, are designed to accurately describe systems of strongly correlated electrons, such as the fully periodic 2D Fermi--Hubbard model. However, as the reference state is compact in momentum space whereas the correlator acts naturally in real space, there is a fundamental mismatch of bases that classical algorithms resolve only by restricting the reference or the correlator. Here we propose a hybrid algorithm in which a quantum processor prepares a low-entanglement momentum-space matrix product state (MPS), precomputed classically by the transcorrelated method at the cost of a nonvariational energy, rotates it to real space, and measures in bases fixed by the Hamiltonian. Because the measurement bases are independent of the correlator, the correlator can be variationally optimized entirely in classical post-processing with no quantum-classical feedback loop. We demonstrate our algorithm on 32 qubits of Quantinuum's H2-2 with a bond-dimension-4 MPS for the half-filled $4 \times 4$ lattice and achieve a relative ground-state energy error of $16 \pm 4\%$ after postselection, reduced to $3.5 \pm 0.5\%$ by calibration using low-order moments from the MPS. Compared with other feedback-free hybrid algorithms, even under generous assumptions, our method requires fewer samples than quantum-selected configuration interaction and fewer two-qubit gates than quantum Krylov methods.

title: PhonoVoxtLM: Exploring Single-Codebook Phonological Tokens for Speech Understanding and Generation
abstract: We investigate how speech token representations can support both understanding and generation within a unified speech language model. We present PhonoVoxtLM, built on the existing VoxtLM framework using phonological tokens designed to retain linguistic content and prosodic information. The existing tokenizer is jointly trained for speech recognition and resynthesis. Its single-codebook units serve as both speech inputs and generation targets, without additional speech-token prediction modules. Experiments show improvements over HuBERT-based baselines across understanding and generation under different training-data scales. Further comparisons with WavLM-based tokens reveal trade-offs between recognition and synthesis, highlighting the importance of evaluating shared representations across both capabilities. We further extend the framework to spoken question answering through fine-tuning with replay. The adapted model improves answering performance over similarly adapted HuBERT baselines while retaining advantages on the original speech tasks. Our findings support single-codebook representations designed for both content and prosody as a practical choice for unified multitask speech modeling.

title: Omni-RS: Unifying Multi-Task Understanding and Generation in Remote Sensing
abstract: Practical remote sensing applications often require both understanding and generation capabilities for the same geographic scene. However, most existing methods address either understanding or generation in isolation, while existing unified remote sensing models' generative ability is limited to text-to-image. To bridge this gap, we propose Omni-RS, a unified framework supporting four remote sensing understanding tasks and five generation tasks. Specifically, we introduce the "Scene-Guided Two-Stage Training" strategy, which first adapts a multimodal large language model to remote sensing understanding and then uses its hidden states to guide a diffusion transformer for image generation. To enable joint learning across diverse generation tasks, we construct UniGen, a unified multi-task generation dataset, by organizing heterogeneous remote sensing data into a unified format. Furthermore, we introduce "Detailed Visual Conditioning", which uses visual conditions encoded by a VAE to guide the generation process, thereby supporting additional generation tasks that require reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Omni-RS performs exceptionally well in understanding tasks and has achieved outstanding results in a variety of generative tasks.

title: Reliable Scale-Free Bandits via Empirical Likelihood
abstract: We study stochastic bandits without knowledge of reward scales or tail parameters. Almost-sure regret guarantees describe eventual learning but do not quantify expected performance or the risk of large regret in a finite run. We introduce $\texttt{EL-F}$, an anytime empirical-likelihood (EL) extension of the $g$-Forcing policy of Cowan and Katehakis (2020), and characterize its performance at three levels. First, for integrable rewards and non-decreasing, diverging exploration schedules $g$ with vanishing increments, $\texttt{EL-F}$ preserves the $g$-Forcing asymptotics for pseudo-regret $R(T)$: $R(T)/g(T)\to\sum_{i:Δ_i>0}Δ_i$ almost surely as $T\to\infty$, where $Δ_i$ is the suboptimality gap of arm $i$. Second, on every sub-exponential instance, for non-decreasing $g(t)=ω(\log t)$ satisfying a mild feasibility condition, expected pseudo-regret is at most $g(T)\sum_{i:Δ_i>0}Δ_i+C_{\underline{P}}$, where $C_{\underline{P}}$ is an instance-dependent constant independent of $T$. Moreover, we also establish finite-time tail bounds with super-polynomial decay in regret beyond the forced-exploration budget. For slowly varying $g$, we determine the exact exponent of linear regret deviations on two-armed Gaussian instances with common variance and establish a matching lower bound among policies satisfying the same expected-regret budget on every such Gaussian instance. These quantitative guarantees also cover the greedy variant obtained at zero EL radius. A fixed positive radius introduces local optimism while preserving the leading asymptotic regret. We establish coupled pathwise dominance over the greedy variant in two-armed bandits with a deterministic suboptimal arm. Experiments demonstrate reductions in prolonged suboptimal allocation compared with $g$-Forcing on challenging instances.

title: Sub-Quadratic Block-Sparse Attention via Odd Binomial Fractal Tree Topologies
abstract: Standard full self-attention in Transformer architectures incurs a quadratic computational and memory complexity, O(N^2), rendering long-context scaling computationally prohibitive. While heuristic and randomized sparse attention patterns alleviate computational overhead, they either suffer from severe context blind spots or introduce stochastic, non-deterministic gradient flows that fail to preserve global associative recall. In this work, we introduce Fractal Block-Sparse Attention, a deterministic, hardware-aligned sparse attention mechanism governed by odd binomial fractal tree dynamics...

title: A Reproducible Simulation Benchmark for Cross-Layer RF Fingerprinting Under Multipath Fading: Comparing Handcrafted Features and End-to-End Learning
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting exploits natural hardware differences between wireless transmitters to authenticate Internet of Things (IoT) devices without cryptography. This paper presents a reproducible simulation benchmark for cross-layer device authentication combining physical-layer (PHY) fingerprints with network-layer behavioral features. IEEE 802.11 short training field preambles are generated for 20 devices, each with a fixed impairment profile (CFO ±50 kHz ≈ ±20 ppm at 2.4 GHz, I/Q gain and phase imbalance, Wiener phase noise, Rapp power-amplifier nonlinearity, DC offset). Every capture passes through an independently drawn six-tap frequency-selective Rayleigh channel and AWGN at a per-capture SNR drawn uniformly from 0 to 30 dB. From each capture a 52-dimensional handcrafted feature vector is extracted. Four PHY classifiers are compared under identical conditions — an RBF-kernel SVM and a deep neural network (DNN) on handcrafted features, a residual 1D-CNN on raw I/Q, and an SVM on PCA-reduced I/Q — with every configuration repeated over 5 independent seeds (3 for the 1D-CNN). The DNN attains the highest accuracy (77.99% ± 4.88, mean ± standard deviation across seeds), ahead of the SVM on the same features (67.33% ± 5.23), the 1D-CNN (58.45% ± 0.78) and the SVM on PCA-reduced I/Q (44.21% ± 5.54); paired, continuity-corrected McNemar tests on identical test partitions find every difference significant on every seed. Accuracy rises monotonically with SNR — from 39.4% (SVM) and 47.6% (DNN) in the 0–3 dB bin to 79.9% and 91.6% at 27–30 dB — and saturates above roughly 16–18 dB. An identity-aligned cross-layer fusion experiment is reported only as an illustrative simulation finding, not as an estimate of real-world performance: a sensitivity analysis shows its apparent gain is set by the within-device variance of the synthetic generator, ranging from +28.9 to −6.2 accuracy points as that variance is swept. All code, the multi-seed harness, the sensitivity analysis and the raw per-seed predictions are openly archived on Zenodo.

title: What Next-Token Surprisal Can and Cannot See: A Registered Null Result on Measuring Narrative Reorganization in a Language Model
abstract: Version 2 (October 2026). An audit found that the registered model, Gemma 4 31B-it, reads plain narrative prose abnormally: about 9 bits per token, against about 3 bits for four other instruct models on the same texts, in two independent implementations. Its surprisal values therefore cannot serve as the measure, and the version 1 results are reported for the record but not interpreted. The measurement code was correct, and the July numbers reproduce exactly. The frozen stimuli were rerun on Qwen3.8 27B, as a declared deviation from the registration. Neither the trigger prediction nor the post-region hypothesis holds (mean trigger contrast −0.48 bits, mean post contrast −0.27 bits, each positive in four of ten pairs). The reversed effect, its repetition mechanism and the calibration account of version 1 are withdrawn. This version adds the audit, the second-model run, the corrected pipeline description and the frozen design document; the stimuli, July data and July code are unchanged. Version 1 remains available. The study tested whether semantic reorganization, the “reveal” moment in which new information reframes previously read material, leaves a measurable trace in per-token surprisal when a language model reads short narrative texts. Ten matched stimulus pairs had byte-identical openings diverging into a reveal or a neutral continuation, and predictions were registered before any data collection. The successor measure registered in version 1, hidden-state distance on identical quoted-back text, is kept unchanged. A plain-language introduction to the measures is given in Bruyn (2026), doi:10.5281/zenodo.23360915. The null is reported in full, per the research program’s standing practice.

title: When Is a Temporal Statement Store a Statement Graph? Export Boundaries for Occurrence Records with Two Clocks
abstract: A temporal statement store keeps every occurrence of a statement as a record. Each record has its own identifier, a triple, a transaction-time lifetime and a valid-time interval, and other records can refer to it. This paper asks which part of such a store can be exported as a Statement Graph without inventing or renaming any occurrence. Statement Graphs are the DAG model behind OneGraph, which lets RDF-star and property graphs interoperate. A record set can be exported this way exactly when it is closed under references and acyclic. Every set contains a largest exportable subset, the export kernel. A linear-time topological peel computes it, and it can be kept up to date with one bit per record. If records are immutable and never deleted, the full history is closed. Exporting it then loses only the cycles that atomic corrections create, and a batch-local check at correction time prevents those as well. Exporting a single snapshot also drops supersession lineage. A dual reference closure keeps that lineage by adding the retracted records it points to. Every omitted record is reported with a reason. The exported history can be written into RDF-star with both clocks stored as reserved statements, and read back without loss. Conjunctive queries over the asserted part return the same answers, up to a quoting bijection. Two alternatives mark the boundary from either side:- RDF 1.2 reifiers export any store, cycles included, but assert per triple rather than per occurrence.- The property-graph branch admits only edges and properties that nothing references. The proofs in the paper are by hand. The validation archive adds:- a Lean 4 development that re-proves the main results;- an executable validator covering exhaustive small stores, random stores and random protocol histories;- traces of both counterexamples through the tiramemsu engine.

title: Governing Large Language Model Services for Confidential Microdata: A Decision Framework for National Statistical Offices
abstract: National statistical offices increasingly face requests to provide large language model (LLM) capabilities in secure research environments. The governance problem is to determine which service configurations, if any, can be supported safely on confidential microdata. These services challenge traditional statistical disclosure control because interaction is adaptive, systems may retrieve documents or call analytical tools, and outputs may appear plausible without being grounded in approved data. This paper proposes a governance framework that organizes each request as a sequence of decisions: whether an LLM is needed, which service mode is justified, which threat model applies, which controls are required, and what evidence must be reviewed before release. The framework spans deterministic pipelines, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-using agents, code-execution agents, linkage configurations, and fine-tuning.

title: Wendt's determinant and finiteness of prime characteristics for permutation binomials
abstract: For $f(X)=X^r(X^s+a)\in\mathbb F_{p^m}[X]$, with $m,r,s\geqslant1$ and $a\in\mathbb F_{p^m}^\times$, put $g=\gcd(s,p^m-1)$. We prove that, for each fixed $g$, only finitely many prime characteristics $p$ admit such permutation binomials, even as $m,r,s,a$ vary. If $6\nmid g$, every such $p$ divides Wendt's determinant $W_g=\operatorname{Res}_X(X^g-1,(X+1)^g-1)$, which is nonzero. When $6\mid g$, this determinant vanishes; inverse power sums and iterated resultants yield an explicit nonzero integer divisible by every such $p>2g+1$. We determine the exact admissible characteristics for $1\leqslant g\leqslant10$, obtain a further divisibility condition over prime fields, and show that in prime fields $g=11$ occurs precisely when $p=23$.

title: CREATE: Creativity Evaluation of VLMs using the Visual Remote Associates Test
abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) are used in creative tasks such as visual storytelling, design ideation, art interpretation, and advertising. Yet we lack principled ways to measure the lateral reasoning of these models compared to human potential. We introduce CREATE, a semi-automatically constructed benchmark containing 155 visual Remote Associates Test problems. These problems require a solver to find an underlying connection among three seemingly dissimilar images. We conduct a human study (N=25) to validate and ground the quality of our benchmark, and evaluate 11 VLMs. Our findings show that most VLMs underperform humans on this task. Our experiments indicate that the associative ability of VLMs depends on the cue concepts provided in the text and does not universally extend to visual puzzles.

title: Over-parameterization Is Neither Robust nor Fragile in Matrix Sensing: A Geometric Theory of Solution Robustness
abstract: Over-parameterization is ubiquitous in modern machine learning, yet its effect on robustness remains poorly understood. We study this question in matrix sensing, a canonical non-convex problem that can also be viewed, under an appropriate parameterization, as training a two-layer quadratic neural network. We develop a rank-aware robustness theory for the Burer-Monteiro factorization when the search rank k may exceed the target rank r_star, thereby capturing over-parameterization. Our analysis shows that robustness depends jointly on the degree of over-parameterization and the local geometry of the attained second-order stationary point: increasing k generally worsens sensitivity, but stationary points with the same search rank can exhibit substantially different robustness. Motivated by this observation, we propose a trajectory-aware algorithm that uses spectral balancing and randomized sketching to steer optimization toward less sensitive solutions. In matrix-sensing experiments, the method reduces paired sensitivity by 18-29 percent for isotropic operators and 87-89 percent for weak-tail operators, without degrading reconstruction accuracy. These results demonstrate that parameter count alone does not determine robustness and identify solution geometry and the optimization trajectory as important levers for improving it.

title: Non-additive symmetric rank-metric codes
abstract: We study non-additive rank-metric codes contained in the space of symmetric matrices over a finite field. Our main focus is on symmetric $2$-codes. For odd $q$, we introduce a quotient construction for $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ in which rank-one differences are described by isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form on $\mathbb F_q^4$. This leads to a correspondence with partial ovoids of the elliptic quadric $Q^-(5,q)$. Using a construction of Cossidente and Pavese, we obtain a non-additive symmetric $2$-code in $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ of cardinality $q^4+2q^3$, improving the previously known general lower bound. We also give an explicit matrix description of this family. Lastly, we present a block-based construction for symmetric $2$-codes that extends the three-dimensional improvement to all odd dimensions. In particular, for every odd $n\geq3$ and every prime power $q>2$, we obtain \begin{equation*} A_q^{\rm sym}(n,2) \ge q^{(n^2-1)/2}+q^{(n^2-3)/2}+q^{(n^2-9)/2}, \end{equation*} which is strictly larger than the maximum cardinality of an additive symmetric $2$-code with the same parameters. This yields the first infinite family (as the matrix dimension $n$ varies) of non-additive symmetric $2$-codes whose size is larger than the largest achievable size of an additive code with the same parameters; before this, such a gap had only been established for $n=3$.

title: StateHarness: Maintaining Evolving Project State for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
abstract: Long-horizon coding requires agents to maintain an evolving view of the project they are changing: what problem is currently being solved, what has already been learned or modified, which other artifacts may be affected, and what work remains unresolved. When this information is scattered across a growing interaction history, local edits can become disconnected from their later consequences and progress can be difficult to carry forward. We introduce StateHarness, a runtime framework that maintains evolving project state without updating model parameters. The working agent records its current problem and hypothesis, important findings and decisions, discovered repository relationships, and unfinished work. Runtime support prompts record updates, searches for callers, tests, and documentation that may be affected by a change, and maintains a compact working brief for subsequent decisions. When behavioral signals accumulate, a separate diagnostic session revisits the recorded history and surfaces overlooked evidence. Across three repository-level evaluations, StateHarness improves task completion and several measures of change consistency. On RefactorBench, full-chain completion increases from 29.4% to 35.3% and cleanup-check accuracy from 87.0% to 95.4%. On five LHTB software-engineering tasks, mean reward improves from 0.427 to 0.576, exceeding LongHorizon-Harness at substantially lower recorded execution cost. On ChainSWE, bug-fix rate increases from 35.1% to 39.5% and residual debt decreases from 60 to 43 items, although pass-to-pass regressions increase. These results show that maintaining project state can improve long-horizon coding while introducing measurable execution and regression trade-offs.

title: Information Limits of Outcome-Resolved Incidence Certification
abstract: Calibrated support observations can constrain a complete quantum instrument without identifying its action by unrestricted tomography. We study what those observations guarantee when the noise law is not supplied. On a fixed four-dimensional incidence-record experiment, we define the set of all complete two-outcome completely positive instruments compatible with the exact raw rejection and outcome probabilities, retaining the classical flags. Exact ideal data identify the target, but an explicit family of complete instruments reproduces the nonzero-data category laws of a low-error contamination device while admitting coherent error of square-root order. A target-ray mass certificate and a common complete-dilation comparison give a universal upper, while an exactly feasible rational instrument supplies a stronger lower witness. At the diagnostic parameter r = 1/300000000, the unhalved target-relative worst-case radius lies between 0.000258065115532250 and 0.000951566242566. The result separates avoidable inequality conservatism from information absent from the measured data. Fixed-functional and fixed-map optimizations have separately certified scopes; they do not solve the global radius. The conclusions are conditional on the supplied carrier, calibration and common-device model. They do not establish an apparatus, device-independent certification, a finite-sample power guarantee or complete formal verification. Selected supporting declarations have one recorded successful Lean 4.19.0 macOS execution and declaration-specific source, type and axiom review; this is not an end-to-end formalization.

Core architecture: Offline-first participatory documentation (with local cryptographic caching) + automated linguistic analysis + generative revival engine (strictly as Augmented Drafting Assistant) + mandatory Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) elder validation + Community Intellectual Property (CIP) enforcement with asynchronous smart contracts + model weight sovereignty protection + intergenerational transmission platform. title: Generation traces for "Beta Gate: Shorter RL Reasoning in Qwen3.5 Without Negative Eigenvalues"
abstract: Raw generation traces behind the paper "Beta Gate: Shorter RL Reasoning in Qwen3.5 Without Negative Eigenvalues" (Avi Fenesh, 2026). One gzipped JSONL file per readout: 229 files, 290,306 traces, 1.40 GB. Each trace holds the item id, the sample index, the reasoning token ids and the answer text at each reasoning budget (256 to 8,192 tokens). No problem text and no gold answers. Covered: Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-2B test reads on MATH-500 and GSM8K (all arms and seeds), validation reads, cap pilots and step 9 curves, the fresh held-out set (AIME 2024 to 2026, AMC 2023, read once), and the mechanism readouts (gate ablation and gate dose) on the GSM8K validation slice. Answers sometimes quote part of a problem statement (173 of the 14,560 4B fresh-set answers at the 8,192 budget quote a span of 80 characters or more); that text stays with its source (MAA for AIME and AMC). The archive comes in 34 parts of 40 MiB (gdn-beta-gate-traces.zip.part00 to .part33). Join them with cat and check the result against SHA256SUMS. The archive unpacks into the layout of the code repository (https://github.com/avifenesh/gdn-beta-gate, tag v1.1.0), next to the readout each file belongs to. There, scripts/rerun_traces.py reruns the five scripts that read generated text (text_stats.py, answer_cap.py, example_traces.py, truncate_curve.py, build_inputs.py) and checks that they reproduce the released outputs. results/TRACES_LEDGER.json lists every file with its trace count and sha256.

title: Performance evaluation and interpretability of a Qwen LangGraph agent for AI written and AI rewritten text detection
abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of large language models has increased the need to distinguish human-authored text from AI-generated content, including cases in which generated text is subsequently rewritten or paraphrased. In practice, many detectors output only a single AI-likelihood score or percentage, offering limited transparency and little indication of whether a passage appears directly AI-written (AIW) or AI-rewritten (AIR). This study presents an agentic detection framework for two connected tasks: binary provenance detection (Human versus AI) and conditional subtype detection (AIW versus AIR). The dataset combined the Human-ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (HC3) and the ai-text-detection-pile with 4,348 pre-generated AIR records produced by a single GPT-based rewriting workflow. The proposed Qwen–LangGraph AI agent was compared to a HashingVectorizer–TF-IDF–SGD classifier, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall, and ELECTRA-small. On the binary test set, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall achieved the best discrimination (99.4995% accuracy and 99.9911% AUROC), whereas the agent achieved 98.8816% accuracy and 99.9187% AUROC. On the AI-only test set (10,769 AIW; 1,274 AIR), the agent obtained the highest threshold-based accuracy (96.7367%), macro-F1 (90.0357%), and AIR F1 (81.8643%), but its AUROC (83.2507%) and AUPR (79.7336%) were lower than those of the DeBERTa-v3-xsmall and ELECTRA-small transformers. Paired DeLong and McNemar analyses with Holm correction showed that the agent improved threshold-based AIR performance over the lexical baseline. Interpretability was operationalised through lexical weights, linguistic and out-of-distribution diagnostics, sentence-level indicators, and route traces. evidence.title: Performance evaluation and interpretability of a Qwen LangGraph agent for AI written and AI rewritten text detection
evidence.abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of large language models has increased the need to distinguish human-authored text from AI-generated content, including cases in which generated text is subsequently rewritten or paraphrased. In practice, many detectors output only a single AI-likelihood score or percentage, offering limited transparency and little indication of whether a passage appears directly AI-written (AIW) or AI-rewritten (AIR). This study presents an agentic detection framework for two connected tasks: binary provenance detection (Human versus AI) and conditional subtype detection (AIW versus AIR). The dataset combined the Human-ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (HC3) and the ai-text-detection-pile with 4,348 pre-generated AIR records produced by a single GPT-based rewriting workflow. The proposed Qwen–LangGraph AI agent was compared to a HashingVectorizer–TF-IDF–SGD classifier, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall, and ELECTRA-small. On the binary test set, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall achieved the best discrimination (99.4995% accuracy and 99.9911% AUROC), whereas the agent achieved 98.8816% accuracy and 99.9187% AUROC. On the AI-only test set (10,769 AIW; 1,274 AIR), the agent obtained the highest threshold-based accuracy (96.7367%), macro-F1 (90.0357%), and AIR F1 (81.8643%), but its AUROC (83.2507%) and AUPR (79.7336%) were lower than those of the DeBERTa-v3-xsmall and ELECTRA-small transformers. Paired DeLong and McNemar analyses with Holm correction showed that the agent improved threshold-based AIR performance over the lexical baseline. Interpretability was operationalised through lexical weights, linguistic and out-of-distribution diagnostics, sentence-level indicators, and route traces. The findings support the use of AI as decision support, not as automated proof of plagiarism or misconduct.

title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Attention-like Selective Reproduction
abstract: Choosing which information to use as the context changes is a basic cognitive operation. We introduce a new task of this kind for quantum reservoir computing (QRC): a binary cue indicates which of two simultaneous input streams the reservoir must reproduce. In simulated spin reservoirs with a trained linear readout, infinitely many measurements (exact expectation values) let the reservoir reproduce the cued stream accurately. At a finite number of measurements \(N_M\), the score exceeds that of a linear readout of the raw inputs only at large \(N_M\) because of sampling noise. Performance increases with both entanglement and coherence in the computational basis, and then saturates. These results show that QRC can select and reproduce a cued stream, and they are a starting point for harder cognitive tasks.

title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration
abstract: This work discusses and tests the potential of reaction graphs for material synthesis, in which events consist of reaction steps (actions) and their outputs (observations). The importance comes from the requirement to synthesize technologically useful materials, especially those that are kinetically stabilized. Often, it is a science that follows years of trial and error, culminating in (published) successful recipes, but is truly driven by far more (unpublished) failures. The entry into the era of AI provides an opportunity to use learning algorithms to encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways, regardless of their technological usefulness, and to decode both forward prediction and inverse learning modes. The main incentive is to accelerate material discovery by generating a global knowledge base that can be shared among data agents and contributed to by them. We will focus on several scenarios in the common synthesis process during solid-state synthesis, primarily because these reactions are kinetic in nature and require closer monitoring and control of the reaction history.

title: SPARCL: Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning in Chest X-ray Analysis
abstract: Pixel-level annotation for chest X-ray (CXR) lesion segmentation is expensive, making active learning (AL) essential. However, existing AL strategies fail to account for the spatial distribution of selected samples, resulting in inconsistent performance across focal (e.g., aortic calcification) and diffuse (e.g., nodules) pathologies. In this paper, we propose SPARCL (Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning) to dynamically balance predictive uncertainty with cumulative spatial coverage. By employing a concave coverage function, SPARCL imposes diminishing returns on previously annotated regions, naturally directing the annotation budget toward under-labeled areas. Furthermore, an entropy gate reverts the algorithm to standard uncertainty sampling when spatial variation is absent. This coverage objective is monotone submodular, guaranteeing near-optimal greedy batch selection. To address how aggregate metrics like Dice obscure regional failures, we further introduce two metrics---Spatial Inconsistency (SI) and Performance Coverage (PC)---to quantify anatomical fairness across AL rounds. Evaluated on an in-house calcification cohort and public CXR benchmarks, SPARCL reaches 95% of fully supervised performance using only 24% of the data, compared to 29% for the best baseline. Ultimately, SPARCL ensures robust spatial reliability, surfacing regional gains that aggregate metrics miss.

title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy
abstract: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. We present Background2Background (B2B), a self-supervised background removal framework leveraging the backgrounds larger correlation relative to the signal. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, transforming signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-based background removal. Across fluorescence, stimulated Raman scattering and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, B2B achieves over 40-fold background suppression and reveals hidden signatures.

title: Aeromagnetic, Radiometric and AAS Elemental Analysis of the Rimin Zayam Area, North-Eastern Nigeria: Implications for Mineral Exploration
abstract: This study presents an integrated interpretation of aeromagnetic, radiometric, and atomic absorption spectrophotometry (AAS) data from the Rimin Zayam area within the Nigerian Basement Complex. High-resolution airborne geophysical data, acquired at 500 m line spacing and 80 m terrain clearance, were processed using Oasis Montaj software to generate Total Magnetic Intensity (TMI), Reduced-to-Equator (RTE), vertical derivative, horizontal gradient, and tilt derivative maps. Radiometric ternary (K-Th-U) imaging delineated lithological boundaries and identified high potassium anomalies concentrated within metatexite migmatites. AAS analysis of ten samples revealed strong positive spatial co-enrichment (r = 0.7133) between aqueous gold and lithium signatures, with a peak Au concentration of 0.101 mg/L and a maximum Li₂O equivalent of 0.562%. The NNE-SSW trending lineaments, identified as the dominant structural trend, control active alluvial tin channels and provide the framework for hydrothermal fluid mobilization. Integration of geophysical lineaments with AAS geochemical anomalies defines five high-priority exploration targets. The study demonstrates that the combination of aeromagnetic structural mapping, radiometric lithological discrimination, and AAS elemental analysis provides an effective multi-parametric approach for mineral exploration in complex crystalline terrains.

title: Tekmerion Spec 003 — claim bundle and assessment (math claims)
abstract: Tekmerion claim bundle for Spec 003 (math claims), bundle version 0.1.1. This is the engineering truth record for one part of the Tekmerion research engine: the claims the spec makes, the test that could prove each claim wrong (its falsifier), the standing of each claim, and the assessment of how the evidence held up. Deposited 2026-10-13 so this record is anchored outside the code repository (red-team follow-up RTE-23 — until now these bundles existed only in the repository). The SHA-256 hashes below are the anchor values: any copy of these files, in the repository or elsewhere, can be checked against them. Files in this deposit: - aee-claims.json — SHA-256 d0ac97bb6b80cebd74e7b1e85feb21da6900d35e65cdcf753fcb786d0224b9c1. The claim bundle: 12 claims (12 draft), each with its falsifier. - aee-assessment.json — SHA-256 7857cb91f21ad7304e9a01d907f3ffb562d78592414938b73cae7a072e9b3c82. The assessment: made after the build; its instruction was to gather more evidence before the claims could be judged, and its summary reads: "Assessed 12 claim(s); found 29 failure mode(s); 10 claim(s) below the 0.70 confidence threshold.". Standing, stated plainly: all 12 claims remain drafts — the after-build assessment found 10 of the 12 below the program's confidence threshold, so this record anchors them as not yet evidenced to the program's standard. The study that exercised this machinery on real 2026 AI-mathematics claims is deposited separately (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23317259).

title: What Makes an AI Character Worth Coming Back To? Humor, Personality, Emotional Connection, and the Art of Meaningful AI Roleplay
abstract: A research-informed design brief, written by the founder of a commercial AI character product (chatbrat.ai), arguing that compelling AI characters are defined by the quality and consistency of the character experience rather than by how explicit they can be. It uses four official chatbrat.ai scenarios to illustrate distinct dimensions (personality and voice, humor, emotional responsiveness, chemistry and pacing, creative initiative, memory and user agency) and proposes a checklist for evaluating them. It is not an independent study and makes no product-performance claims. No benchmark results are reported.

title: Retraction Note: Mamba-fusion for privacy-preserving disease prediction
abstract: After publication, concerns were raised regarding misrepresentation of datasets and that claims are not supported by the data. The descriptions of the ECG, EEG, clinical, and demographic data in the paper are inconsistent with the sources of this data. Furthermore, it is impossible to demonstrate that the approach that fuses data across modalities works, if the datasets derive from different individuals. Several references (3, 10, 29, 41, 44, 46, 53, 69, 73) appear to be irrelevant to the overall topic.

title: Using emojis to uplift emotion: Effects on mental health chatbots’ performance
abstract: As AI-based chatbots increasingly expand access to mental health support, understanding how text-based systems convey emotional attentiveness without face-to-face nonverbal cues is important. Emojis may serve as lightweight paralinguistic cues, yet their effects in mental health support remain unclear. Drawing on the Stereotype Content Model and psychological ownership theory, this study examines associations between emoji use and users’ emotional well-being, satisfaction, and continuance usage intention. Two scenario-based online experiments were conducted in China using random sampling through Credamo, yielding 459 valid responses (59 in the pretest and 400 in the main study). Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26 and the PROCESS macro. Across the experiments, emoji use was associated with more favorable emotional well-being, satisfaction, and continuance usage intention. Mediation analyses supported an indirect pathway through perceived warmth and psychological ownership, whereas the corresponding competence-based pathway was not supported. AI literacy strengthened the perceived warmth–psychological ownership association but, contrary to predictions, weakened the perceived competence–psychological ownership association. Moderated mediation analyses provided preliminary support for AI literacy strengthening the warmth-based indirect effects of emoji use on emotional well-being and continuance usage intention. The corresponding effect on satisfaction was not supported. These findings extend research on AI-mediated mental health support by identifying a warmth–psychological ownership pathway and the differentiated role of AI literacy. The study also offers preliminary, context-bounded guidance for the strategic and context-sensitive use of emojis in supportive, non-clinical chatbot interactions.

title: Trust Before Autonomy: Rethinking Agentic Remote Sensing for Crisis Response
abstract: Agentic remote sensing is evaluated on how many questions it can answer, whereas crisis response depends on whether its answers can be relied on and how much of the decision can safely be handed to the agent. This paper argues that \emph{autonomy should be earned, not assumed}: An Earth-Observation (EO) agent should be granted autonomy in proportion to demonstrated reliability, epistemic honesty and verifiability. The position is supported by an evidential meta-analysis of twelve agentic RS/EO/GIS benchmark studies from peer-reviewed venues. Only one repeats runs, three contain unanswerable tasks and none measures calibration. Their own tables show that completed workflows are often not correct (task success exceeds tool-call correctness by up to 54pp on identical queries), that the gap to an expert trajectory widens overall with trajectory length (from 7 to 56pp), and that capability does not predict abstention (Spearman r from -0.25 to 0.50, all n.s.). The paper then contributes three EO-specific trust properties, an autonomy ladder for crisis EO tasks, and a readiness protocol that replays archived emergency activations before any live use. In this context, current evidence justifies assistive roles only.

title: Prompt or Policy? Optimizing Physician Slate Presentations with LLM User Simulators
abstract: Choosing the right physician is a key challenge for patients seeking medical care. Physician recommendation systems identify relevant doctors, but patients still find it difficult to compare their profiles to make a decision. We formulate slate presentation optimization: given a patient's medical case and a fixed, ranked list of physicians, we generate short, case-specific summaries that make doctors easier to compare, while remaining grounded in the information in their profiles. To optimize physician presentations without relying on real patient interactions, we develop an offline framework that uses persona-conditioned LLMs to simulate patient choices. We generate patient personas from attributes extracted from each medical case and evaluate presentations for factual accuracy, relevance, naturalness and simulated patient choice. We also use a second LLM judge, unseen during optimization, to assess simulator-specific overfitting. We compare automatic prompt-level optimization with GEPA, parameter-level optimization with GRPO, and their combination across two model sizes. GRPO substantially outperforms GEPA in satisfying the full set of constraints, and its gains in simulated conversion persist under the unseen judge. GEPA alone brings smaller improvements, but using its optimized prompt to initialize GRPO speeds up training and achieves the highest simulated conversion. These results show that prompt-level and parameter-level optimization play complementary roles in improving how physician recommendations are presented.

title: Extending Layered Attestation into ARM Application Run-Times
abstract: Modern mobile and edge platforms provide hardware-backed attestation of application and platform integrity at load-time. However, they offer little support once application execution begins. We present ARA, an Application-Runtime Anchor for ARM that extends this load-time chain of trust into execution. ARA bootstraps from the underlying ARM platform Root of Trust (RoT) through a measured loading chain and establishes an attested protected run-time within the application address space using recently introduced ARM Permission Overlay Extensions (POE). The resulting run-time domain can host programmable RoTs for Measurement and Storage (RTM/RTS), enabling application run-time integrity verification, attestation evidence generation, and protected use of secrets while retaining efficient access to application run-time state. As exemplary uses, we instantiate ARA for protected media decryption and application control flow measurement. Our prototype and evaluation show that ARA supports frequent run-time RoT-backed operations at near in-process cost, with roughly 10x and 50x lower overhead than out-of-process equivalents. This offers a practical bridge from layered attestation to application run-time trusted computing on ARM.

title: CIPHER Forecast 001: Three Mathematical Convergence Predictions Following the October 2026 AI Mathematics Expansion
abstract: TITLECIPHER Forecast 001: Three Mathematical Convergence Predictions Following the October 2026 AI Mathematics Expansion CREATORAlannah Sheridon Nightingale DATE2026-10-09 VERSION1.0 RESOURCE TYPEPreprint / Technical report / Forecast ABSTRACTThis forward forecast applies CIPHER, a structural comparison framework authored by Alannah Sheridon Nightingale, to identify three mathematical convergence directions following the October 2026 expansion of machine-generated mathematics. The forecast concerns (1) stronger use of code-to-lattice and lattice-to-code transfer mechanisms in sharp bounds and optimality results, (2) direct links between stability quantities in disordered-system landscapes and algorithmic, learning, jamming, or satisfiability thresholds, and (3) convergence between computation embedded in incompressible Navier-Stokes flow and classical regularity quantities such as vorticity growth, enstrophy, derivative control, or related coercive functionals. Each forecast includes an explicit failure condition and is frozen as Version 1.0 for later append-only evaluation. KEYWORDSCIPHER; mathematical forecasting; coding theory; lattice geometry; error correction; E8; spin glasses; perceptrons; jamming; satisfiability thresholds; Navier-Stokes; fluid computation; regularity; vorticity; enstrophy; structural convergence DESCRIPTION / NOTECIPHER and its associated framework remain the intellectual work of Alannah Sheridon Nightingale. Publication of this forecast, or use of computational assistance in preparing it, is not intended to transfer, assign, or license CIPHER to OpenAI or any other party. Implementation details of CIPHER are not disclosed in this publication. EVALUATION HORIZON2028-12-31 VERSION CONTROLVersion 1.0 is intended to be frozen after publication. Later results should be appended as evaluations rather than used to alter the original predictions.

title: FOCUS: An Adaptive Fractional Graph-Diffusion Attention Operator, with a Preliminary Hallucination-Warning Application
abstract: Hallucination in autoregressive language models arises when generation dynamics enter a locally stable but factually unsupported attractor. We propose FOCUS (Fractional Order Confidence for Uncertainty Signalling), a framework that replaces the fixed-geometry softmax attention kernel with the adaptive fractional graph-diffusion operator Aαl,h,t=exp(−τL^αl,h,t), where L^=I−D^−1/2P^D^−1/2 is the symmetrised normalised attention Laplacian of the causal prefix graph of each generation step (spectrum in [0,2], proved without assuming double stochasticity of P^) and αl,h,t∈(0,1) is a differentiable control variable predicted per layer l, head h, and generation step t. The key mathematical result is that for μk<1 (low-frequency modes), higher αl,h,t leads to less attenuation (more energy passes through), while for μk>1 (high-frequency modes), higher αl,h,t leads to more attenuation. By assuming that grounded evidence is low-frequency on the attention graph, high αl,h,t is thus advantageous in both spectral regimes simultaneously. The per-head specialisation of αl,h,t arises not from a static spectral tradeoff within a single head but from a training-dynamics competition between the LM loss (which rewards structural diversity across heads, including low-αl,h,t heads that pass high-frequency syntactic features) and the hallucination penalty. Because this penalty pushes αl,h,t down at hallucinated tokens, it trains αl,h,t as an indicator of hallucination rather than as a protective mechanism, and we state what this implies for the interpretation of the experiments. We prove the complete spectral theory, the causality of the construction, and the Fréchet derivative, along the admissible score-induced family of prefix Laplacians for which the zero eigenvalue stays structurally pinned, of the composite map L^↦exp(−τL^α), via the Daleckii–Kreĭn formula with a spectral-gap-dependent bound, and provide a direct Lanczos strategy for computing exp(−τL^α)v with measured error and cost. The warning mechanism is the spectral imbalance statistic It=α¯tctx/(α¯tnoise+ε), whose drop precedes hallucination onset by 6–7 tokens on hallucinating sequences in preliminary synthetic experiments. We also identify spectral localisation analysis—verifying that hallucination spans concentrate in high-frequency modes of the attention graph—as the critical empirical validation for the framework. The evidence assembled here supports FOCUS as a well-founded spectral operator and a preliminary hallucination-warning statistic; establishing it as a protective decoding mechanism, as the acronym’s original reading suggested, is left as an open empirical target .

title: FedLCD: A Federated Learning Framework with Layer-Wise Consistency Detection
abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data, but it is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks, in which malicious clients upload manipulated model updates to disrupt training or degrade model accuracy. Existing Byzantine-robust aggregation methods typically operate at the whole-model level, making them less effective against partial-layer attacks and causing potentially useful information from unaffected layers to be discarded. To address this, we propose a Federated Learning framework with Layer-wise Consistency Detection (FedLCD). Specifically, we design a layer-wise Byzantine robust aggregation algorithm that detects malicious updates by computing pairwise cosine similarities at the granularity of individual layers, and retains only those with higher average similarity. This design filters malicious updates while preserving benign information from unaffected layers. Theoretical analysis confirms that FedLCD achieves a convergence rate of O(1/T), where T denotes the total number of communication rounds. This rate matches that of standard FedAvg, while FedLCD guarantees Byzantine robustness when benign clients constitute the majority. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that FedLCD achieves accuracy comparable to or higher than existing baselines across various Byzantine attack scenarios, while maintaining robust detection performance, particularly under partial-layer attacks.
