title: PADO-Pauli: A GPU-Accelerated Implementation of Pauli Propagation
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms utilize parameterized circuits many times during training, at new parameter values, over batches of data, and with gradients. Pauli propagation approximates the expectation values of such circuits classically by evolving the observable in the Heisenberg picture as a truncated sum of Pauli strings. We present PADO-Pauli, a GPU engine for Pauli propagation that compiles a circuit and its observables once into sparse matrices in which each rotation angle contributes only a cosine and a sine factor, so every later evaluation reuses the compiled program. It evaluates batches of parameters and data inputs embedded as rotation angles. By default its gradients come from a vector-Jacobian product registered with PyTorch's automatic differentiation, so they flow through the angles to any classical layer that produces them. PADO-Pauli also provides truncation by Pauli weight and coefficient size, and noise channels. Zero-filtering removes terms that do not contribute to an expectation value in the all-zero reference state and makes the batched forward pass about 1.5 times faster. Compared to cuPauliProp on an NVIDIA A100, PADO-Pauli evaluates up to 10 times faster on 4 to 12 qubits and uses up to 3.1 times less memory on 16 qubits. We check its accuracy against exact statevector simulation up to 28 qubits. These features make PADO-Pauli a practical toolkit for training variational quantum algorithms, including quantum machine learning models.

title: LULA I: Rollback-Resilient Hash-Based Signatures with Cache-Accelerated Signing
abstract: LULA is Ring0 Labs’ research family of hash-based signature schemes. LULA I produces 5,720-byte signatures. With a 72 MiB signing cache, median signing takes 3.59 ms for 32-byte messages; median verification takes 0.12 ms. Loading a saved cache and producing the first signature takes 5.70 s median. After complete cache loss, three first-signature runs took 330–338 s. The paper examines these memory–latency tradeoffs and compares measured implementations. Rollback-security transfer is conditional; full reference-signer security remains open. Contact: angel@r-0.org Published by Lugel Labs

title: THE RUSSIAN-UZBEK PARALLEL CORPUS AS A FOUNDATION FOR MACHINE TRANSLATION: THE CURRENT STATE OF RESEARCH
abstract: Abstract. This article reviews contemporary research on Russian–Uzbek parallel corpora and their use in machine translation. It examines the concept of a parallel corpus, the stages involved in its compilation, principles of data collection and cleaning, text segmentation and alignment, and morphological and syntactic annotation. Particular attention is paid to the linguistic characteristics of the Russian–Uzbek language pair, including differences in morphology, word formation, and syntax. Current corpus resources, software tools, and neural-network approaches are also reviewed. The article demonstrates that the quality of Russian–Uzbek machine translation is directly related to the volume, representativeness, and linguistic processing of parallel data. Keywords: Russian–Uzbek machine translation; parallel corpus; corpus linguistics; neural machine translation; morphological analysis; alignment; low-resource language.

title: Efficient training-free query routing framework for federated retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses in external documents retrieved at inference time. In federated RAG (FedRAG), documents are distributed across multiple autonomous corpora that cannot be centrally aggregated due to privacy, regulatory, or organizational constraints. A key challenge in FedRAG is query routing: selecting a subset of relevant corpora for each query without broadcasting to all participants. Existing routing approaches rely on supervised learning, requiring a uniform retrieval embedding model across corpora and costly retraining whenever the federation changes. These assumptions violate corpus autonomy and limit scalability in dynamic federated environments. We propose RAGSpot , a training-free query routing framework that enables efficient corpus selection without requiring a shared local retrieval embedding model. RAGSpot represents each corpus using compact cluster-level metadata derived from its vector index and estimates corpus relevance via query-to-cluster matching. In addition, it introduces a rank-based fusion strategy that jointly leverages document-level and corpus-level rankings to support robust aggregation across heterogeneous embedding models. Experiments with corpora from the BEIR benchmark show that RAGSpot improves retrieval accuracy over the strongest training-based router by 1.23– \(1.48\times\) in nDCG and 1.28– \(1.66\times\) in Recall, and over the strongest LLM-based router by 1.63– \(2.01\times\) in nDCG and 1.93– \(2.34\times\) in Recall, without any further training. Also, RAGSpot achieves query latency that is comparable to, or even lower than, that of SOTA methods on average.

title: First-order Optimization Methods with Generalized Smoothness for Low-rank Matrix Factorization
abstract: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.

title: Euclidean Distance-Based Flow Matching
abstract: Flow Matching has recently become popular as a technique for generative modeling with applications in many domains. In the standard Flow Matching formulation, we interpret the vector field as the solution of a least-squares regression problem, which is known to be sensitive to contamination. Therefore we leverage the viewpoint of robust statistics and replace the squared Euclidean distance with the Euclidean distance as a regression objective. This seemingly minor change strongly affects the properties of Flow Matching. We provide a probabilistic interpretation of the new regression target as a conditional geometric median and use this characterization to study distributional robustness of the Euclidean Distance-based Flow Matching. We analyze the mathematical properties of this changed objective and the effect of a contaminated target distribution on the involved conditional velocity distributions. We discuss the challenge of directly characterizing the distribution that our method induces. In specific contamination settings we show theoretically that our method yields an improvement for severe contamination. Finally, we present numerical experiments conducted on the CIFAR-10 image dataset where a proportion of the samples has been contaminated. Our Euclidean distance-based Flow Matching shows a clear advantage in scenarios of severe contamination of the target distribution.

title: Unsupervised and Supervised Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 2)
abstract: Since the rise of supervised deep learning modelet dets, researchers has attempt to solve infrared small targection using various models like conventional neural networks, GANS, Transformers, Mixture of Experts and recent graph/hypergraph neural networks. Moreover, these deep neural networks methods surpassed the traditional unsupervised models and the low-rank and sparse decomposition unsupervised models reviewed in "Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1). In this context, the aim of this paper is to provide a complete survey of the deep learning models in infrared small target detection. First, we categorize the different approaches found in the literature in terms of the modeling models of strategies. Then, we have discussed them in terms of the critical situations that they claim to handle. Furthermore, we present the specific performance evaluation. Then, we conclude with several promising directions for future research.

title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
abstract: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while keeping the encoder fixed. We evaluate RAN-JEPA using public operator performance data for pretraining and a real-equipment four-cell 5G testbed for domain adaptation, post-training, and control. Across four future 15-minute intervals, RAN-JEPA achieves lower action-conditioned prediction error than a GPT-2 world-model baseline and a mechanistic rule, while remaining close to a strong persistence reference. What-if evaluation further shows that the model produces distinct and coherent future trajectories under matched SLEEP and KEEP plans. In closed-loop control, RAN-JEPA consistently supports higher sleep ratios than the two baselines at comparable congestion cost. These results show that observation-first, action-conditioned learning can turn abundant passive telemetry and limited intervention data into a practical predictive model for energy-aware RAN control.

title: One Voice, One Impression: Why Customers Perceive the Service Quality of AI Voice Bots Holistically and What It Means for Electronic Commerce
abstract: AI voice bots are a standard channel for post-purchase service in electronic commerce, yet conversational-agent research has centered on text chatbots, and whether the quality dimensions of a voice agent are perceived as separate remains open. This study argues that customers experience the agent as one unified impression, because a voice-first encounter is a continuous spoken dialogue without a visual interface, so customers respond to the agent as a single social actor. Perceived quality is theorized as a higher-order construct, building on information systems success theory, technology acceptance theory, and social responses to computers, and tested on a cross-sectional survey of 295 voice bot users in Israel across eight service categories, with partial least squares structural equation modeling and competing measurement models. The quality facets remain distinguishable, yet one general factor accounts for most of their common variance, supporting a single higher-order construct. Perceived quality is the strongest predictor of overall service quality, directly and partly through perceived usefulness, while interaction complexity shows no significant moderating or predictive effect. Because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, these relationships are associations, not demonstrated causal effects. The study extends success and acceptance theory to the voice-first service encounter.

title: Similarity-Guided Graph Learning with Embedding-Space Oversampling for Anomaly Detection in Heterophilic Cryptocurrency Transaction Networks
abstract: The rapid development of cryptocurrency has led to an urgent demand for anomaly detection targeting illegal transaction activities. Cryptocurrency transaction networks have two core characteristics: class imbalance and connection heterophily. Existing anomaly-detection methods tend to cause over-smoothing of anomaly nodes’ features and have low recall rates for anomaly nodes, resulting in poor detection performance. Although some studies have noticed these challenges separately, there is still a lack of a unified solution framework. This paper proposes a cryptocurrency anomaly-detection framework specially designed for cryptocurrency transaction scenarios. It consists of three core modules: Heterophily-adaptive Aggregation Module, Generation-based Minority Class Oversampling Module, and Ensemble Anomaly-Detection Classifier. The Heterophily-adaptive Aggregation Module enables the framework to resist heterophily noise during learning node embeddings by adaptively adjusting the aggregation weights of neighboring nodes. The Generation-based Minority Class Oversampling Module augments the learned minority node embeddings in the embedding space to obtain a more balanced class distribution. Finally, the Ensemble Anomaly-Detection Classifier is used to predict the detection result. Experimental results on multiple cryptocurrency transaction datasets show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional machine learning methods and mainstream graph neural network models.

title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. Finally, we identify opportunities for future research in unified dynamic annotation, efficient spatial reasoning, standardization of evaluation, expanded spatial range, and human-centered spatial interactions.

title: LongForcing: Scaling Temporal Manifold Matching for Long-Horizon World Rollout
abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models have emerged as a foundation for long-horizon world rollout. However, when extended far beyond their training windows, these models suffer from progressive drift: visual quality deteriorates, motion becomes inconsistent, and object identity gradually collapses as generated frames are recursively reused as context. We study a supervision-horizon gap: short-horizon distillation leaves later rollout states without direct supervision. We show that matching short-window marginals need not determine long-horizon behavior, while longer on-policy trajectories expose delayed failures to training. This motivates temporal manifold matching at scale for long-horizon world models. Building on this insight, we introduce LongForcing, a distillation approach that scales teacher supervision to long student self-rollouts. LongForcing preserves the short-horizon teacher-forcing and causal ODE-distillation stages, while replacing the realscore teacher in the final distribution-matching stage with an extended-horizon bidirectional teacher. The long-horizon teacher supervises extended student self-rollouts using the standard distribution-matching formulation, without modifying the student architecture or increasing inference cost. We evaluate LongForcing on text-to-video generation and interactive action-conditioned world models, achieving a VBench Quality score of 85.52 and improving WorldRoamBench 60s action score by 23.9 points in first-person ablations. Qualitative stress tests further sample interactive rollouts up to 24 hours, far beyond the training horizon. These results suggest that scaling supervision along the temporal axis is a practical step toward long-horizon world models. The project website and code are at https://github.com/Fantasy-AMAP/LongForcing.

title: Auditing Explanation Faithfulness in Privacy-Preserving Federated Intrusion Detection: code and results
abstract: Code, configurations, per-run results, per-sample attribution and faithfulness files, model checkpoints, summary tables, figures and the full deviation log for the article "Auditing Explanation Faithfulness in Privacy-Preserving Federated Intrusion Detection" (F. Şahin, N. S. Mert). The study audits the faithfulness of post-hoc explanations (Integrated Gradients, GradientSHAP, attention rollout) under formally accounted differential privacy (DP-SGD) and Byzantine-robust aggregation in federated intrusion detection on ToN_IoT and the corrected CICIDS2017 release. The datasets themselves are not redistributed; README.md explains how to obtain them and reproduce every table and figure. Code: MIT licence. Results, tables and figures: CC BY 4.0.

title: Topological Foundations for an Autonomous Cognitive Seed Kernel: An Early-Stage Empirical and Logico-Mathematical Prototype (The Complete 42-Asset Evidentiary Corpus)
abstract: This monograph details an initial, exploratory attempt to formalize the mathematical, physical,and semiotic architecture of an Artificial Intelligence Seed Kernel. Contemporary large-scalemachine learning relies predominantly on ungrounded statistical token prediction trained overmassive brute-force parameter spaces, resulting in extreme thermodynamic inefficiency, catastrophicforgetting, and a total decoupling from physical boundary invariants.As a corrective, this work investigates an alternative hypothesis: that an autonomous, scale-invariant cognitive kernel can be bootstrapped from a finite, unalterable corpus of foundationalinvariants. We convene forty-two primary physical, mathematical, epigraphic, and topological sourceassets—partitioned into the 30-document R_Positronium Set and the 12-asset L_PositroniumSet—to demonstrate that stable cognitive inference operates not via discrete Turing tape steps, butthrough continuous energy minimization across an inward-curving topological medium.By synthesizing balanced ternary radix arithmetic, non-Euclidean planar metrics, discreteparity-violation mechanics, non-equilibrium quantum statistical thermodynamics (Lindblad/NESSdissipation), distributed consensus algorithms, and multi-scale acoustic waveguides, we outline theparameters of an engine capable of high-density semantic resonance. title: How Underdog Brand Biography Mitigates Consumer Skepticism Toward AIGC: Evidence from AI-Generated Agricultural-Product Advertisements
abstract: While AIGC can improve operational efficiency in marketing, it may also erode consumer trust owing to widespread skepticism toward AIGC. Therefore, this study examines agricultural product advertisements to explore the impact of Underdog Brand Biography (UBB) disclosure on consumers’ purchase intentions. It also investigates the mediating roles of cognitive trust and affective trust, as well as whether these effects differ across product-price levels and production-background conditions. We conducted three experiments to investigate these relationships. The data were analyzed using t-tests, analyses of variance, and moderated mediation models. The findings indicated that UBB disclosure significantly increases purchase intention and that this effect is mediated by both cognitive trust and affective trust. The indirect effects via both pathways differed across product-price levels: both were significant in the high-price condition, whereas in the low-price condition only the affective pathway remained significant. Additionally, both trust pathways were amplified in the cultivation-scene background condition relative to the plain background condition. Given that our samples were drawn from an online consumer panel, the present findings and their implications should be interpreted with respect to online consumer populations. These findings provide preliminary insights that may inform trust-based theories of AI disclosure and offer practical considerations for marketers designing AIGC advertising strategies.

title: Fine-Tuning Shifts Form Before Competence: Treatment-Correlated Style Drift Confounds Surface-Form Evaluation of Adapter Specialization
abstract: Stacking task adapters on a frozen domain adapter is a common approach for modular specialization of large language models, usually justified by knowledge injection; whether the surface-form graders standard in this setting can measure such specialization validly has remained unexamined. Two challenges follow: isolating the domain layer’s marginal contribution under identical task training, and determining whether measured differences reflect competence or output form. In this work, both are addressed with a matched-arm DoRA ablation on a frozen Qwen 3.5 9B hybrid: a 242 M-parameter domain expert is trained on a licensed 27.8 M-token corpus, and byte-identical task adapters are trained flat, stacked (DFE-stacking), and jointly across three tasks and five conditions, with the key extraction pair replicated at a second training seed; every grader is audited by per-item failure classification and a dual-rater blind human re-grade with consensus adjudication. The principal finding is that fine-tuning shifts output form before competence: stacking yields no seen-task benefit; an apparent generalization collapse on an unseen schema reduces to a single, highly seed-stable formatting coercion that the domain layer dampens and task-mixture training eliminates, and most automated keyword-grading failures prove to be correct paraphrases, leaving no genuine capability loss detected on any instrument. Because such style drift is induced by the training condition itself, surface-sensitive grader error becomes bias aligned with experimental arms rather than noise. Three additional experiments extend the findings: the coercion replicates on Llama 3.1 8B (60% vs. 19% untuned); a pre-registered 240-item formatting-perturbation battery across four further unseen schemas and eight conventions reveals fine-tuned conditions ranking lowest under strict grading yet highest under format-normalized grading; and a matched-compute wrong-domain control shows the domain layer’s coercion dampening to be generic substrate regularization, while value integrity under the induced drift tracked the substrate’s domain. The principal contribution lies in the identification and quantification of this confound: surface-form evaluation of adapter specialization is structurally confounded, and per-item audits of the type released herein are a necessary component of specialization studies.

title: Out of Tune: How Different Fine-Tuning Methods Affect Information Security
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) enables task specialization but introduces privacy risks through training data memorization. Practitioners deploying fine-tuned LLMs in sensitive domains such as medicine, law, and finance must choose among fine-tuning methods without clear guidance on the privacy implications of that choice. We compare full fine-tuning, partial fine-tuning, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) by measuring how much sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) each method leaks from training data, using planted canaries to track memorization. Six Llama configurations (3B and 8B parameters) are evaluated across the medical, legal, and finance domains under three extraction attack types: prefix attacks, random prompting, and completion attacks. Full fine-tuning leaks the most on average, followed by LoRA. Partial fine-tuning leaks the least in every configuration we tested, though the relative ordering of full fine-tuning and LoRA varies. Contrary to our initial hypothesis, LoRA's parameter efficiency does not yield the strongest privacy protection; we attribute this to LoRA's architectural breadth across all transformer layers. The performance-privacy trade-off these findings expose has direct consequences for deployment. Even partial fine-tuning on the 3B model, our best configuration, leaked canaries, so practitioners should assume some leakage by default.

title: Explicit constructions of ternary plateaued functions with maximal algebraic degree
abstract: Plateaued functions with high algebraic degree play a significant role in cryptosystems. We find nine explicit construction methods for ternary plateaued functions with (almost) maximal algebraic degree . To obtain the methods, we first consider a framework for constructing ternary functions, which are good candidates for plateaued functions. Then we obtain three explicit criteria for input values of the framework for the ternary functions to be s ′ -plateaued functions, where s ′ = s − 1 , s , or s + 1 . Consequently, we find nine explicit construction methods for ternary s ′ -plateaued functions, which arise from s -plateaued functions, where s ′ = s − 1 , s or s + 1 . The connection with the degree bound is also given. Using our construction methods, we find three infinite families of ternary 1-plateaued functions with (almost) maximal algebraic degree; this is done by selecting out input functions from partial spread bent functions. We emphasize that eight of our construction methods are new and that these three infinite families are also new to the literature.

title: Neural Supervised Clustering for Learning Individualized Treatment Rules with Many Treatments
abstract: Learning an individualized treatment rule (ITR) with many treatments requires estimating treatment-specific effects from limited observations per arm. Treatments with similar conditional responses can share information, but linear contrast models may miss nonlinear heterogeneity. We propose nonlinear supervised clustering fusion (NSCF), a neural Q-learning framework with a shared nonlinear covariate representation and low-dimensional treatment embeddings. Pairwise fusion groups treatments with similar learned contrasts, yielding an ITR and an interpretable partition. An alternating algorithm combines neural training, embedding fusion, validation-based partition selection, and unpenalized grouped refitting. NSCF lowers regret relative to a strong neural reference in nonlinear exact-sharing simulations; perturbations characterize the limits of hard sharing. In a melanoma xenograft application, NSCF improves average policy value over the neural reference. These results support nonlinear representation learning with supervised treatment fusion when treatment effects exhibit shared structure.

title: Machine--human agreement in marking undergraduate assignments is specific to model, prompt and institution
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) promise to automate one of higher education's most resource-intensive activities: assessing student writing. Existing evaluations are typically limited to a single model, a single prompt and a single institution. Using 761 undergraduate psychology assignments from three UK universities, we evaluated three frontier LLMs, individually and in ensemble, on accuracy, prompt sensitivity, error independence, generalisability and evidential basis. Agreement between human and machine marks varied widely, with no model or prompt optimal across institutions. All models compressed marks towards a common central tendency, overvaluing the weakest assignments and undervaluing the strongest. Because this error was shared, ensembling failed to remove it. Machine marks also rewarded linguistic features more strongly than human marks. Since human-machine agreement was a joint product of model, prompt and institution, we conclude that current LLMs lack evaluative capacity transferable across contexts, and that single-context validation overstates readiness for deployment.

title: Mining Correlated Motifs with Wildcards in PPI Networks: Exact and Optimal
abstract: A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network is a graph whose nodes are protein sequences and whose edges represent physical interactions between proteins. Correlated Motif Mining (CMM) seeks pairs of sequence motifs whose co-occurrence in interacting proteins reveals binding sites and interaction mechanisms. Formally, in the $(\ell,d)$-CMM problem, we are given a graph $G=(V,E)$, with $V\subseteqΣ^*$ for an alphabet $Σ$, and integers $0\leq d<\ell$, and we seek a pair $\{X,Y\}$ of motifs, each of length $\ell$ and containing $d$ wildcards, that maximizes a support measure $f(G,\{X,Y\})$; e.g., the count $f_E$ of edges $\{u,v\}\in E$ such that $X$ matches a substring of $u$ and $Y$ matches a substring of $v$, or vice versa. Although existing approaches have produced biologically meaningful results, they are either inefficient or heuristic-based, as the underlying optimization problem is NP-hard. Here, we revisit $(\ell,d)$-CMM. For $d=0$, we give an exact $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$-time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$-space algorithm, where $N$ is the total length of the node strings, and prove that this time is conditionally optimal under the Strong Exponential-Time Hypothesis. For any $d>0$, we give an exact $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\binom{\ell}{d}^2N^2\right)$-time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$-space algorithm, and observe that the problem is W[1]-hard parameterized by $d$. The latter algorithm improves the state of the art by exponentially large factors in both time and space. We further demonstrate experimentally that our algorithms are practical on real-world PPI networks and find significantly higher-scoring motif pairs than the state of the art. Moreover, we show that our algorithms find many top-scoring motif pairs that the state of the art misses entirely. Taken together, our results suggest that exact CMM with wildcards is more tractable in practice than previously assumed.

title: Beyond Belief Nesting: Rethinking Higher-Order Theory of Mind in Large Language Models
abstract: Theory of mind (ToM), the ability to reason about others' mental states, underlies effective communication and coordination. Its higher-order form enables reasoning over nested perspectives in strategic interactions. However, existing evaluations often equate belief-nesting depth with reasoning order, allowing nominally higher-order questions to admit lower-order shortcuts. We formalize effective order through the distinct events supporting successive belief prefixes, revealing widespread order inflation across existing benchmarks. We introduce HopToM, with certified full-order questions and controls for lower-order alternatives. Under direct prompting, mean accuracy across four frontier LLMs falls from 73.5% at first order to 20.0% at fourth order, and human participants also struggle. Causal interventions link a recurring class of errors to evidence for shallower belief prefixes. We introduce HopTrace, a plug-and-play inference-time method that encodes each interaction once into perspective records and resolves nested queries deterministically. On certified narrative questions, it improves fourth- and fifth-order accuracy by 22.0 and 38.5 percentage points over strong prompting baselines, while using 20-39 times fewer tokens than multi-call methods. These results sharpen how higher-order ToM is evaluated and offer a practical way to improve perspective reasoning in interactive agents.

title: Risk-Averse Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment with Finite-Sample Guarantees
abstract: Inference-time alignment steers diffusion models toward downstream objectives without costly fine-tuning, but existing methods typically optimize expected cost (or reward) without explicitly controlling tail risk. In this work, we propose a risk-averse framework for inference-time alignment of diffusion models that balances expected cost and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) under trajectory-level Kullback-Leibler regularization. We characterize the optimal path distribution and reverse transitions as functions of the CVaR threshold, reducing the alignment problem to a one-dimensional optimization problem over the threshold. We show that this one-dimensional optimization problem can be nonconvex in general, establish sufficient conditions for convexity, and introduce quadratic regularization to enable efficient derivative-free ternary search. Under suitable assumptions, we provide finite-sample guarantees for threshold optimization and value estimation, and combine them into a terminal total-variation bound relative to the regularized target under exact resampling. Experiments on synthetic data and image generation using Stable Diffusion demonstrate improved tail performance over risk-neutral baselines while maintaining competitive average cost.

title: Detect and Correct: A Survey of Hallucination Detection and Mitigation in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can produce fluent text that is false, unsupported, or inconsistent with supplied evidence. This behavior limits their use in knowledge-intensive and high-stakes applications. This critical narrative survey organizes hallucination management as a detect-and-correct control loop: generate a response, decompose it into verifiable claims, estimate risk or retrieve evidence, and then accept, revise, regenerate, or abstain. Detection methods are classified by access requirements into white-box, grey-box, black-box, and evidence-grounded families; mitigation methods are grouped into training-time, inference-time, and post-hoc interventions. Its central synthesis is that system reliability depends on the weakest pipeline stage and cannot be inferred from detector accuracy alone.

title: Enhancing Energy Efficiency with Explainable AI: A Study in Smart Building Heating Load Prediction
abstract: Artifical intelligence (AI) is a powerful tool for Achiving sustainable development goes. However, the complexity of any AI models possess the significant changes in the locals such as energy management. This paper expores the application of outstanding articulated intellectuality (xAI) techniques to enter the transparency and resolution of the machine learning models used for predicting energy consumption in smart buildings. Using a database containing structural and physical features of buildings, a pre-active model was developed based on the Random Forest regression algorithm. To interpret and explore the model’s preferences, two xAI methods - LIME and SHAP - were applied. The results demonstrate that both xAI techniques effectively identify the key features influencing load projections,thereby providing eligible insights into energy-saving strategies. Furthermore, the combination of machine learning and xAI methods forters trust and accounting in AI-driven energy management systems.

title: Pareto optimization of textual and engagement features for crime-related social media analytics
abstract: Crime-related social media content provides valuable information for situational awareness and policy support; however, engagement-driven signals, such as likes and retweets, can introduce popularity bias and affect predictive outcomes. This study proposes a fairness-aware, Pareto-based, multi-objective optimization framework for feature selection and Random Forest hyperparameter optimization, leveraging textual and engagement features. A dataset of 32,000 crime-related tweets covering Fraud, Accident, and Murder was represented using TF-IDF and interaction-based features. Four optimization strategies, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (ERL), and Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), were comparatively evaluated. NSGA-II jointly maximized classification performance while minimizing a fairness penalty based on Statistical Parity Difference (SPD), Disparate Impact (DI), and Equality of Opportunity Difference (EOD). In this study, fairness refers to mitigating engagement-driven popularity bias across behavioral user groups rather than demographic discrimination. NSGA-II achieved an accuracy of 0.8118 and an F1-score of 0.8051, with an SPD of 0.08, DI of 0.97, and EOD of 0.06, demonstrating the most favorable balance between predictive performance and behavioral fairness. Although removing engagement features improved standalone Accuracy and F1-score, retaining them enabled explicit assessment and mitigation of engagement-driven bias. Stratified cross-validation and comparative analysis across the optimization strategies further supported the consistency of the observed results. The findings demonstrate that integrating fairness objectives directly into Pareto-based optimization provides a practical and interpretable approach to balancing predictive effectiveness and engagement-driven fairness in crime-related social media analytics.

title: Complete classification of weight-3 logical operators in the Face Centered Cubic lattice CSS code
abstract: The $$[[3L^3, 2L^3{+}2, 3]]$$ CSS code on the Face Centered Cubic (FCC) lattice reaches a 67.7% encoding rate with weight-12 stabilizers. Its distance is 3. We classify every weight-3 logical operator of the code. The X-type ones are the $$4L^3$$ triangular faces of the lattice. The Z-type ones are the $$4L^3$$ claws, each formed by the three edges of a tetrahedron meeting at one of its vertices. The two families are exact duals under the exchange of vertices and octahedral voids, and each spans $$2L^3 - 1$$ independent logical classes. We prove this count analytically from the homology of the 3-torus, not only numerically: the cycle space has dimension $$\tfrac{5}{2}L^3 + 1$$ , the boundary space has dimension $$\tfrac{5}{2}L^3 - 2$$ , and subtracting the stabilizer rank leaves $$2L^3 - 1$$ for every even L. So $$k = (2L^3 - 1) + 3$$ , and the excess rate is carried entirely by weight-3 operators. We then show that this sector cannot be protected. The three-body parity $$Z_{e_a}Z_{e_b}Z_{e_c}$$ at a face anticommutes with four octahedral stabilizers, so it is not measurable, and no measurement of any kind can distinguish $${|{\psi }\rangle }$$ from $$\hat{L}_T{|{\psi }\rangle }$$ for arbitrary encoded $${|{\psi }\rangle }$$ . Removing the sector requires adjoining all $$2L^3 - 1$$ independent directions, which returns $$k = 3$$ . Verified exactly over GF(2) at $$L = 4, 6, 8, 10$$ .

title: Leakage benchmarking with decohering subgroups in the presence of preparation and measurement errors
abstract: A common problem with physical qubits is that the state can leak outside the computational subspace. To characterize the problem, it is desirable to measure both the leakage probability and the fidelity of gates inside the computational subspace. Randomized benchmarking is a readily accessible method for estimating average gate fidelities and can be modified to account for leakage. However, in the presence of state preparation and measurement errors (SPAM) there are parameter degeneracies, and fidelities and leakage become underdetermined. We study the example of qudits with any number of leakage levels under the assumption of gate-independent noise. We show that randomized benchmarking sequences with leakage level decoherence can be analyzed as a Markov process with noisy classical preparations and measurements. This result generalizes to randomized benchmarking with random gates from an arbitrary group that contains a phase-decohering subgroup. We characterize the parameter degeneracy in inferring the Markov process, preparations and measurements. Based on this characterization we develop a measurement and inference method taking advantage of known conservative bounds on SPAM to constrain fidelity, leakage and other parameters of the Markov process, state preparations and measurements. As part of our study, we experimentally implemented the measurement method for a qubit defined on the one-excitation subspace of two transmons, for which there are two leakage levels. We determined confidence intervals accounting for parameter degeneracy for a number of performance parameters of the system. For leakage and fidelity, we compare these intervals to those obtained for several conventional methods for leakage benchmarking.

title: Linear regression with probabilistic networks for network-linked data
abstract: Network-linked data combine a network with covariates and responses observed for its nodes. Common regression approaches either model dependence among neighboring responses using the observed network or capture similarities associated with network structure without explicitly modeling response dependence. We propose a probabilistic network-linked data analysis framework that incorporates both features while accounting for randomness in network formation. The model uses normalized connection probabilities to weight peer responses and latent positions to capture network cohesion. A two-step likelihood procedure first estimates the network structure and then fits the response model. We establish theoretical guarantees for network recovery in sparse networks with heterogeneous node effects, and prove consistency and joint asymptotic normality of the regression estimators subject to suitable conditions. The analysis also clarifies when estimating the network preserves the classical convergence rate for spatial autoregressive models. Simulation studies demonstrate the estimation performance of the method and assess its inference accuracy. An analysis of diplomatic network data illustrates its practical application.

title: Personalising Deformable Image Registration with Clinical Context and Deformation History for Adaptive Radiotherapy
abstract: Adaptive radiotherapy must account for anatomical changes during treatment, but doing so depends on reliably mapping targets, organs at risk and dose across serial images. Existing registration methods treat each image pair independently, without using radiotherapy-specific context or the patient's preceding anatomical trajectory. We developed Clinical-context-Aware and Patient-adaptive Deformable Image Registration (CAP-DIR), integrating source contours, dose, clinical text and prior-registration features. We evaluated 16,361 CT examinations from 3,473 patients across four institutional cohorts and five public benchmarks. CAP-DIR increased internal-test organ-at-risk-region normalized cross-correlation from 84.76% to 96.92% relative to the strongest learning-based comparator, with low deformation folding, and remained superior across seven external cohorts. In a blinded review of 20 longitudinal cases, clinically acceptable contours increased from 45.0% to 82.5% for clinical target volumes and from 22.5% to 62.5% for organs at risk, while estimated editing time decreased. In a controlled benchmark, CAP-DIR reduced global dose-mapping error by 34.5% relative to the strongest comparator. These findings show that clinically informed, longitudinal registration can improve contour usability and dose mapping for adaptive radiotherapy.

title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
abstract: Large language models increasingly generate Solidity smart contracts that, once deployed, can never be patched, making a single latent fault permanent and exploitable. Yet current evaluations mostly ask only whether generated code compiles. We introduce SolBehave, a benchmark for evaluating the correctness of model-generated contracts at scale, moving beyond ad hoc unit tests. Across 250 real, reproducible Ethereum contracts, we apply three complementary tests of behavioural fidelity: differential fuzzing, historical-transaction replay, and, as our core contribution, synthetic-transaction replay guided by a Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graph that enumerates the space of legitimate function-call sequences. Differential fuzzing compares each generated function with the original on automatically generated inputs; historical replay compares the whole contract on the transactions it actually received on-chain; DCR-guided replay compares it on sequences of calls that follow its intended usage, including orderings that never occurred on-chain. We evaluate seven state-of-the-art open-weight models after one round of automated repair. Compilation success ranges from 26.4% to 92.7%, but under differential fuzzing only 31.4% of all generated function bodies that compile, pooled over models and samples, are equivalent to the original. Divergence at the contract level is the norm rather than the exception: for six of the seven models, between 13% and 31% of the generated contracts that compile diverge from the original under historical replay, and between 13% and 44% under DCR-guided replay; only Gemma-4-31B stays below 3% on both. Compilation is therefore a necessary condition for correctness and far from a sufficient one.

title: Resource-based reliability of quantum-coherent devices
abstract: Quantum devices can lose the resource needed for a specified function without entering a fixed failure subspace. We propose a resource-based reliability framework for this situation, quantifying the remaining task-relevant resource relative to a stated ideal capacity. The resource measure is selected through its operational connection to the task and the allowed operations. We develop this approach for a trusted quantum random-number generator and a calibrated two-port interferometer. Relative-entropy coherence determines the optimal asymptotic yield of standard coherent qubits under incoherent operations for the former, while logarithmic $l_1$ coherence quantifies the fringe resource of the latter and determines its calibrated correct-port probability. An exactly solvable multi-spin spin-boson model illustrates how environmental records affect these resources at the same isolated-spin dephasing strength. Collective noise preserves coherence within magnetization sectors for product inputs, but enhances the decay of Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger branch coherence. Finite-record simulations connect the resource definitions to measurement counts and show that increasing the sample size reduces statistical fluctuations without eliminating bias from an incorrect many-spin noise model. The resulting framework provides a task-specific route to reliability assessment when a fixed failure projector is insufficient, while keeping retained resource capacity distinct from a classical survival probability.

title: Dynamic Interpolation for Training-Time Prediction Reshaping in Low-Light Image Enhancement
abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is an important image/video processing problem for reliable visual systems under poor illumination, yet it remains challenging due to the strong coupling among insufficient illumination, noise amplification, and structural degradation. Existing methods typically rely on sophisticated network architectures or engineered objective functions. While effective, the former increases model complexity and deployment burden, whereas the latter relies on empirically tuned loss weights. We revisit supervised LLIE from a training-dynamics perspective and observe that brightness-related errors tend to converge early, while residual noise and structural artifacts often remain insufficiently optimized in later stages. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based LLIE backbones show that DITM consistently improves fidelity and perceptual quality while preserving the inference-time architecture and introducing no additional inference-time computation.

title: NetCoFi: A Budget-Aware Coarse-Fine Dual-Branch Model for Encrypted Traffic Classification
abstract: Encrypted traffic classification is critical for network management and security, but practical deployment must balance classification accuracy and inference cost. Existing models typically process fixed flow windows with limited control over computation after training, which can limit the accuracy-efficiency trade-off under constrained resources. To address this problem, we present NetCoFi, a budget-aware classifier that allocates computation at coarse and fine granularities. Using byte representations and observable packet metadata, NetCoFi selects token neighborhoods for fine-grained encoding while compressing the full window into complementary coarse context. Multi-budget training enables the same model to operate at different routing budgets without retraining. Evaluation on six public datasets shows that NetCoFi achieves state-of-the-art classification performance when trained from scratch. Under low-budget settings, NetCoFi improves average Macro-F1 by 7.86 percentage points across three datasets, compared with a same-depth static baseline. In a DPDK-GPU traffic processing pipeline, it increases mean batch throughput from 26.42 to 43.42 Mb/s, a 1.64x improvement over NetMamba.

title: KRIPTOGRAFIYA VA RAQAMLI XAVFSIZLIK: MA'LUMOTLARNI HIMOYA QILISH UCHUN MATEMATIK USULLARDAN FOYDALANISH
abstract: Kriptografiya va raqamli xavfsizlik zamonaviy axborot jamiyatining ajralmas tarkibiy qismi bo‘lib, ma’lumotlarni himoya qilishda matematik usullardan keng foydalanishni nazarda tutadi. Ushbu yo‘nalishning asosiy maqsadi — axborotning maxfiyligi, yaxlitligi, mavjudligi va ishonchliligini ta’minlashdan iborat. Kriptografiya yordamida ma’lumotlar maxsus algoritmlar orqali shifrlanadi va faqat ruxsat etilgan foydalanuvchilar tomonidan ochilishi mumkin bo‘ladi. Bu jarayonda ochiq va yopiq kalitlar tizimi, simmetrik va asimmetrik shifrlash usullari, xesh funksiyalar hamda raqamli imzo texnologiyalari qo‘llaniladi. Matematik nuqtai nazardan, kriptografiya sonlar nazariyasi, modul arifmetikasi, algebraik tuzilmalar va ehtimollar nazariyasiga tayanadi. Masalan, katta tub sonlar bilan ishlash, diskret logarifm muammosi yoki faktorlashtirish kabi murakkab masalalar kriptografik tizimlarning mustahkamligini ta’minlaydi. Shu sababli, kriptografik algoritmlarni buzish amaliy jihatdan juda qiyin bo‘lib, bu esa ma’lumotlarni himoya qilishda yuqori darajadagi ishonchni kafolatlaydi. Raqamli xavfsizlik esa kriptografiyadan tashqari kengroq tushuncha bo‘lib, u tarmoqlarni, qurilmalarni va dasturiy ta’minotni himoya qilishni ham o‘z ichiga oladi. Bu sohada foydalanuvchilarni autentifikatsiya qilish, ruxsat darajalarini boshqarish, zararli dasturlardan himoyalanish va kiberhujumlarning oldini olish muhim ahamiyatga ega. Bugungi kunda internet orqali amalga oshiriladigan bank operatsiyalari, elektron tijorat, bulutli texnologiyalar va davlat xizmatlarining xavfsizligi aynan kriptografik va raqamli himoya mexanizmlariga bog‘liq. Shuningdek, raqamli xavfsizlik inson omili bilan ham chambarchas bog‘liq bo‘lib, foydalanuvchilarning xavfsizlik madaniyatini oshirish muhim vazifa hisoblanadi. Kuchli parollardan foydalanish, shaxsiy ma’lumotlarni himoya qilish va shubhali manbalardan saqlanish kabi oddiy choralar ham katta ahamiyat kasb etadi. Umuman olganda, kriptografiya va raqamli xavfsizlik ma’lumotlarni himoya qilishning ishonchli vositasi sifatida doimiy rivojlanib borayotgan va yangi tahdidlarga moslashib kelayotgan ilmiy-amaliy sohadir.

abstract: Code, CPT derivation, and experiment notebooks accompanying the manuscript "Quantum Bayesian Network Inference for Pipeline SCADA Threat Detection on NISQ Hardware," submitted to the ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering. title: System analysis approaches for the development of advanced architectures
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has established a new technological and organizational landscape across all industries, yet the process of creating AI architecture remains disjointed, intuitive, and domain-oriented. The proposed study introduces a System-Analytical Framework of Artificial Intelligence Architecture Design (SA-AI Framework), a collection of principles from systems analysis and multi-criteria decision-making intended to harmonize architectural design processes across heterogeneous AI domains. The paper is based on twenty-five current studies in explainable AI, neural-symbolic architectures, human-centered robotics, agentic systems, and domain-specific applications, such as healthcare, finance, energy, and education, that inform a comparative synthesis of architectural design principles. A Research Design Science Research (DSR) approach is used to model and test the SA-AI Framework conceptually across four stages: requirements analysis, identification of architectural alternatives, multi-criteria evaluation, and model validation. Results show that the framework offers a systematic, defensible method for constructing AI architectures, enabling greater exposure, flexibility, and decision-making effectiveness. It has cohesively unified the different models of AI, including the agentic AI, Explainable AI (XAI), Human-Centered AI (HCAI), and safety-driven architectures, providing both theory and practice to AI engineering and policy design. This paper concludes that system analysis helps design AI systems that integrate both technical and socio-technical systems to enhance the governance, reliability, and sustainability of intelligent architecture in the next generation.

title: Diabetes Risk Prediction under Severe Class Imbalance: Comparing Firth Logistic Regression and SMOTEN-Based Logistic Regression
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a major noncommunicable disease, and reliable early-detection prediction can support Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 3.4. This study compares standard logistic regression, Firth's Penalized Logistic Regression, and SMOTEN-based logistic regression for diabetes risk prediction under severe class imbalance using Wave 5 of the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS5). The analysis included 115 respondents, comprising 8 diabetes cases (6.96%), with all predictors represented as categorical variables. Model performance was evaluated using 50 repeated stratified 75/25 train-test splits, with SMOTEN applied only to training data to prevent leakage. Standard logistic regression failed to converge across all partitions. Firth's Penalized Logistic Regression identified waist circumference as significantly associated with diabetes status (odds ratio = 10.69, 95% CI: 1.5673.14) and achieved mean accuracy of 89.17%, sensitivity of 8.00%, specificity of 95.19%, and AUC of 0.692. SMOTEN-based logistic regression achieved accuracy of 86.90%, sensitivity of 12.00%, specificity of 92.44%, and AUC of 0.632. Brier scores were 0.089 and 0.098, respectively, compared with 0.064 for the prevalence benchmark, indicating poorer overall probabilistic prediction performance. These findings illustrate the challenges of rare-event prediction under severe class imbalance and highlight the need for larger samples and further validation before clinical application.

title: The Gap Is in the Geometry: A Convergent Meta-Analysis of Multi-Facet Aerial and Remote Sensing Video Understanding
abstract: Aerial and remote sensing video is increasingly evaluated like web video, by posing multiple-choice questions to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) over sampled frames and reporting accuracy. This paper argues that this recipe measures the wrong aspect, and supports the claim with a convergent meta-analysis of a broad set of published results, organized in four evidence tiers, in which a claim becomes a position only when collected evidence agrees. Parameter scale exhibits a median of +3.4 accuracy points per tenfold increase on aerial benchmarks, far below a human gap of at least 19 points, whereas acquisition conditions control perception, as 315 of 318 evaluations in 19 within-paper contrasts lose accuracy when conditions such as altitude, view, object size or time horizon become harder. No aerial benchmark in the corpus combines video input with per-task human and random baselines, competence collapses from answering to acting in closed-loop navigation, and the same MLLMs score higher on the aerial benchmark than on ground spatial ones, but lower on studies that test cross-view geometry. From these findings the current study derives five falsifiable principles and proposes the AVU-Card, a reporting card for aerial video benchmarks

title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Gauge-equivariant graph neural networks generate ordered products of gauge links through local message passing, but the geometry of these internal structures is not captured by the receptive field alone. We investigate the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks generated by recursive node- and edge-feature operations, independently of network training. Analytical and numerical results reveal a separation between rapid growth of contour length and much slower spatial expansion: deeper compositions generate increasingly long paths through repeated traversal of relatively compact regions. Loop expansions of fermionic observables provide a physical interpretation of this hierarchy, showing how spatial locality remains compatible with high-order dependence on nearby gauge fields. These findings identify complementary roles of network depth in extending spatial reach and enriching the representations constructed within that reach, providing a geometrical perspective on learning lattice gauge observables.

title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.

title: Linear Regression Beyond Covariance: Latent Slope Spectra from Higher-Order Cumulants
abstract: Least squares summarizes the joint distribution of a response and regressor through second-order information. When an observed regressor is composed of latent components carrying different relationships with the response, this summary can average over distinct linear effects. We study the additional linear information contained in higher-order mixed cumulants and formalize it through the latent slope spectrum. Ordinary least squares is a variance-weighted barycenter of this spectrum, whereas higher-order cumulants can separate its components when the spectrum is sufficiently parsimonious. In the scalar one-confounder model, fourth-order cumulants identify the unordered pair $\{β,β+γ\}$ through a $2\times2$ linear system and a quadratic equation. We develop estimation and root-$n$ inference under regular separation and show that detection and estimation diverge near degeneracy: slope multiplicity remains detectable on an $n^{-1/4}$ local scale even when the individual slopes are not uniformly regularly estimable. In multiple regression, a quadratic tensor recurrence yields a test of one versus multiple effective coefficient vectors that does not require the vectors themselves to be identified; multiplicity can therefore be consistently detectable even when the recurrence operator is noninjective. The same quadratic diagnostic can retain signal in directions where a first-order higher-cumulant restriction cancels exactly. The results distinguish representation, identification, detection, and estimation of latent linear heterogeneity, while making explicit the limits of structural and causal interpretation from observational data alone.

title: GRLoRA v2.1 - multi-task LoRA conflict-diagnosis pipeline and figure-generation code
abstract: Code accompanying the study Diagnosing Conflict-Mitigation Regularizers in Multi-Task Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: A Leakage-Controlled Educational Benchmark and an Evaluation Protocol. Contents. code/main/ - data construction (build_data_v2.py, prepare_v2_1.py), readiness gate, joint multi-task LoRA training (train_v2.py), validation evaluation under the heterogeneous-task protocol (evaluate_v2.py), loss and penalty definitions (regularized_loss.py), summary-table builders and offline attribution analysis. code/root/ - run driver helpers. analysis/ - extracts tidy CSVs from the run artifacts and renders the manuscript figures. environment/ - Python, pip freeze, nvidia-smi and key library versions. Reported runs. 4x NVIDIA RTX A4000 (16 GB), Python 3.9.12, torch 2.8.0+cu128, transformers 4.57.6, peft 0.17.1, base model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, 400 optimisation steps, batch size 4, LoRA rank 8. Exact per-run commands are recorded in the companion deposit in each run's run_config.json. Documented traps. Supplying --rho overwrites lambda_orth as rho * lambda_shared, so an "orthogonality only" run must pass --lambda_shared 0 with --lambda_orth and no --rho. A shell variable collision silently corrupted the grouping argument in an earlier revision.

title: Measuring LLM Self-Checking Fairly: Data and Results (Anonymous Review Artifact)
abstract: Review artifact for a paper on measuring what a language model's check of its own answer does. It holds the side-blind answer key (the final answer each response settles on and whether it is right), the human labels (four rounds), the final result files behind the tables and figures, and the analysis scripts, with a script that rebuilds the numbers from saved outputs. Model responses, raw judge replies, the trained reader weights and the training code are withheld during review and will be released on acceptance. See README.md for the map from paper items to files.

title: Slice-Aware Adversarial Vulnerability Analysis of TabNet-Based Intrusion Detection in 5G Network Slicing
abstract: A TabNet-based network intrusion detection system can achieve 97% global accuracy while simultaneously exhibiting near-total adversarial collapse in the URLLC slice (PSRI = 0.023)—a critical vulnerability that conventional metrics entirely conceal. This paper introduces the Per-Slice Robustness Index (PSRI) and Slice-Weighted F1 (SW-F1) to expose such hidden vulnerabilities in 5G network slicing environments, and proposes Attention-Guided Evasion (AGE), a transfer-based adversarial attack that exploits TabNet’s native attention mask to concentrate perturbations on the most influential features. Using the CICIoT2023 dataset with 34 attack categories mapped to eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC service slices, we demonstrate that AGE achieves a 50.2% accuracy drop at ε=0.10 while using 17× less L2 perturbation than FGSM and modifying only 8.5% of features. The proposed metrics expose a 0.121-point gap between global weighted F1 (0.928) and slice-balanced SW-F1 (0.807), demonstrating that conventional evaluation systematically overestimates protection for minority slices in heterogeneous 5G environments. These findings highlight the necessity of slice-aware adversarial evaluation frameworks for 5G network security.

title: Risk-Adaptive Behavioral Attenuation via Episode-Latched Policy Gating and Bounded Relearning for Deployed Reinforcement Learning Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning behaviors can become harmful after deployment even when the policy is unchanged, a risk existing methods address mainly before or during training rather than through reversible correction. This paper proposes a risk-adaptive attenuation framework for a frozen context-conditioned policy encoding validated nominal and safe endpoint behaviors. Recurring harm is identified through evidence accumulation, and a severity-aware selector applies gradual, accelerated, or hard-switch attenuation latched for the full episode. Verified probes support bounded relearning, and recurrent harm reactivates the intervention. The selector is a fixed rule, and only the base policy is trained with reinforcement learning. Evaluation uses Risk Corridor, a stochastic-cost gridworld, with ten policies tested across fixed, mixed, and noisy-observation conditions against shield and Recovery RL baselines. Under mixed-severity deployment the selector reached a final hazard rate of 0.00 and task completion of 1.00 at a safety cost of 3.98, above hard switching (2.83) and Recovery RL (0.00). Deviation cost was 44.36, versus 61.20 for Recovery RL (27.5% lower) and 27.81 for the shield, which completed only one of three phases. The framework is best described as a safety–utility trade-off rather than superior safety. Mode-selection accuracy remained above 0.96 at 0.10 observation noise, safety and reversibility held across all tested conditions, and aired differences were consistent for at least nine of ten policies, reaching the exact test’s minimum attainable significance (p=0.00195) for four of five comparators.

title: Programlama Dillerinde Bellek Güvenliği ve Ağ İletişimi: Rust, Go, Haskell ve Diğer Modern Dillerin Siber Güvenlik Odaklı Karşılaştırmalı ve Ampirik Analizi
abstract: Bankacılık, telekomünikasyon (5G/6G), savunma sanayii ve nesnelerin interneti gibi kritik altyapılar büyük ölçüde yazılıma bağımlı hâle gelmiştir; bu yazılımların güvenilirliği ise bellek güvenliği ve eşzamanlılık doğruluğu gibi düşük seviyeli garantilerle doğrudan ilişkilidir. Bu çalışma, ağ iletişimi ve siber güvenlik bağlamında kullanılan programlama dillerini bellek güvenliği modeli, performans, ekosistem olgunluğu ve geliştirme ekonomisi açısından karşılaştırmaktadır. Çalışma üç bağımsız veri kaynağına dayanmaktadır: on bir dilde yürütülen kontrollü mikro-ölçüm deneyi, büyük ölçekli bir geliştirici anketinin (n = 49.191) ham mikro-verisi ve kurumsal geçiş literatürü. Ölçümler, Rust'ın sahiplik modelinin tahsis yoğun iş yüklerinde Go'nun çöp toplayıcısından yaklaşık 1,8 kat daha hızlı olduğunu, makine koduna derlenen dillerin soğuk başlatmada JVM'e kıyasla yaklaşık 16 kat daha hızlı olduğunu ve ağ katmanında Rust'ın hem gecikme hem verim bakımından C ile aynı düzeyde kaldığını göstermiştir. Anket analizi, Rust'ın %72,5 ile en yüksek sadakat oranına sahip olmasına karşın fiili kullanımının %9,6'da kaldığını ortaya koymuştur. Bulgular, tek bir dilin tüm senaryolar için en uygun seçenek olmadığını, bileşen sorumluluğuna göre seçilen karma (polyglot) mimarinin en dengeli sonucu verdiğini göstermektedir. Türkiye alt örnekleminde C'nin kullanım oranı küresel ortalamanın 1,65 katı iken Rust'ın oranı küresel düzeyde kalmaktadır. Çalışma, Türkiye için kademeli bir geçiş yol haritası önermektedir.

title: Lightweight Two-Stage Secure Boot with Automatic Rollback for STM32 IoT Devices
abstract: Secure firmware updates are critical for embedded and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, as any failure during the update process can render the system permanently unavailable. Existing secure boot solutions often depend on dedicated hardware security modules or offer only limited recovery mechanisms, which are impractical for low-cost, resource-constrained microcontrollers. This study presents a novel architecture for safe boot using a lightweight two-stage system withautomatic rollback features, implemented on an STM32 microcontroller. The system allocates security and update functions between two bootloaders (BL1 and BL2) via a metadata-governed state machine and dual-bank flash memory, thereby obviating the need for supplementary hardware. We have implemented common security protocols within this framework, including AES for encryption, SHA-256 for integrity verification, and RSA-2048 for authentication. We also added a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP)-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) system to safeguard data transmission over UART. Experimental results conducted on the STM32-F746 IoT hardware platform showed that the proposed solution achieved significant efficiency in boot data recovery across diverse error scenarios and effectively thwarted unauthorized attacks and system degradation. The performance parameters for total system boot delay ranged from 5 to 15.5 seconds, while public key authentication latency consistently remained below 258.8 ms. The suggested methodology is appropriate for IoT devices that use low-capacity microcontroller units, such as STM32 platforms. The findings validate that resource-limited IoT devices can attain strong security and assured system resilience without the need for specialist hardware.

title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
abstract: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. However, this task becomes increasingly challenging under adverse environmental conditions, such as poor weather and low lighting, where the performance of state-of-the-art pre-trained object detectors and on-board sensors tends to degrade, which limits their effectiveness and reliability. Moreover, retraining models for each operating context imposes significant constraints due to high data requirements, computational resources, and time. Considering this, we propose a novel context-aware multimodal late fusion approach that integrates a lightweight gating network within our probabilistic calibration framework. The gating network extracts environmental context and dynamically modulates the detection outputs of pre-trained object detectors based on the inferred context, without retraining of the detectors. Our methodology is evaluated on a modified KITTI dataset, in which the camera images and lidar pointclouds are augmented for varying fog levels. Experimental results show that our approach yields an approximately 14% relative improvement over non-adaptive late fusion baselines, achieving a consistent average precision of 56% across different fog levels.

title: Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1)
abstract: Infrared small target detection is often used in different civilian and military applications to detect static or moving targets in scenes like in ground, air and sea surveillance. First valuable research has emerged since 30 years ago and the two last decades witnessed very significant publications in this field following the rise of low-rank and sparse decomposition (model-based methods) and deep learning models (data-based methods). Furthermore, several surveys can be found in the literature but none of them addresses an overall review in this field. In this context, the aim of this paper is to provide a complete survey of the traditional and recent approaches in infrared small target detection. First, we categorize the different approaches found in the literature in terms of the modeling models, i.e mathematical models, machine learning models and signal processing models. Then, we have discussed them in terms of the critical situations that they claim to handle. Furthermore, we present the available resources, datasets and libraries. Then, we conclude with several promising directions for future research. For the sake of reading, this survey is divided into two parts: 1) "Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1)" about conventional and low-rank and sparse decomposition (model-based methods), and 2) "Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 2)" about deep learning models (data-based methods).

title: Analisis Pengaruh Parameter Contamination dan N_estimators Terhadap Performa Isolation Forest Dalam Deteksi Anomali Transaksi Keuangan
abstract: Deteksi anomali pada transaksi keuangan merupakan proses penting untuk mengidentifikasi aktivitas yang menyimpang, terutama pada dataset yang bersifat tidak seimbang. Salah satu algoritma yang banyak digunakan adalah Isolation Forest, namun performanya dipengaruhi oleh konfigurasi parameter, khususnya contamination dan n_estimators. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kedua parameter tersebut terhadap kinerja Isolation Forest menggunakan dataset transaksi kartu kredit yang terdiri dari 284.807 data. Dataset dibagi menjadi data latih dan data uji dengan rasio 80:20 serta dilakukan standarisasi menggunakan StandardScaler. Pengujian dilakukan menggunakan beberapa kombinasi nilai contamination dan n_estimators, kemudian dievaluasi berdasarkan Precision, Recall, F1-Score, dan ROC-AUC. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa parameter contamination memberikan pengaruh lebih besar terhadap keseimbangan Precision dan Recall dibandingkan n_estimators. Kombinasi n_estimators 300 dan contamination 0.002 menghasilkan performa terbaik dengan Precision sebesar 0.2675, Recall 0.3096, F1-Score 0.2871, dan ROC-AUC 0.9455. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa pemilihan parameter yang tepat mampu meningkatkan kinerja Isolation Forest dalam mendeteksi anomali pada data transaksi keuangan.Kata Kunci: Contamination; Isolation Forest; N_estimators; Parameter Tuning; Transaksi Keuangan

title: Fractal Knowledge Trees for Provability-Guided Multi-Agent Learning
abstract: We introduce Fractal Information AI, a proof-of-concept framework for structured knowledge representation and selective multi-agent learning. Knowledge is represented by recursively nested tree structures whose nodes carry uncertainty, entropy-like information measures, and a model-defined provability score. A Learning Efficiency Measure (LEM) combines these quantities to prioritize knowledge updates, while a cross-agent flux term represents exchange of information between agents. The framework is formalized through node utility, network-level learning-efficiency measures, stochastic update equations, and decision-impact functions. Synthetic simulations illustrate the resulting dynamics, including selective node prioritization and the appearance of highly connected or influential nodes. These simulations should be interpreted as demonstrations of the internal behavior of the proposed model rather than as evidence of superiority over neural, reinforcement-learning, or knowledge-graph baselines. A central clarification of this audited formulation is that “provability” denotes a model-level score unless a node is explicitly linked to a formal language, axiom system, and proof procedure. Gödel incompleteness therefore motivates caution about formal closure but does not itself provide a learning metric or establish limits for contemporary statistical AI. The paper identifies the formal definitions, benchmark comparisons, ablation studies, calibration procedures, and energy measurements required to convert the present conceptual architecture into a validated learning method.

title: Private Banking Analytics and Synthetic Data Generation
abstract: This Python program demonstrates how a bank can prepare protected repayment-profile statistics and synthetic records for an external analytics partner. It processes the complete public UCI credit-card dataset, limits each customer's contribution, and uses OpenDP to release two noisy contingency tables under a combined pure-DP budget of ε=1. Non-negative projections give the tables a common private total, while Private-PGM generates 10,000 synthetic records from the noisy measurements. The program derives an age-group dashboard, withholds proportions with insufficient noisy support, and evaluates synthetic-data accuracy separately using the public source. A persistent ledger and cache prevent identical requests from generating fresh noise or refitting the model. Checks verify cache reuse without data access, preservation of released files, and rejection of changed requests requiring additional budget review.

evidence.title: Private Banking Analytics and Synthetic Data Generation
evidence.abstract: This Python program demonstrates how a bank can prepare protected repayment-profile statistics and synthetic records for an external analytics partner. It processes the complete public UCI credit-card dataset, limits each customer's contribution, and uses OpenDP to release two noisy contingency tables under a combined pure-DP budget of ε=1. Non-negative projections give the tables a common private total, while Private-PGM generates 10,000 synthetic records from the noisy measurements. The program derives an age-group dashboard, withholds proportions with insufficient noisy support, and evaluates synthetic-data accuracy separately using the public source. A persistent ledger and cache prevent identical requests from generating fresh noise or refitting the model. Checks verify cache reuse without data access, preservation of released files, and rejection of changed requests requiring additional budget review.
