title: Particle Reallocation Search for hyperparameter tuning of particle filters
abstract: Abstract. Particle-filter performance depends strongly on model- and algorithm-side hyperparameters. Exhaustive offline procedures, such as grid search, are computationally expensive because every candidate configuration is compared through a filtering run that uses the target number of particles N over a long time horizon. We propose Particle Reallocation Search (PRS), a hyperparameter search that operates under a fixed total computational cost and treats the number of particles as a controllable resource. Following the successive-halving idea used for hyperparameter optimization in machine learning, PRS first screens many candidates with small ensembles and discards poorly scoring candidates at intermediate screening times. The released particles are then reallocated to the surviving candidates by deterministic duplication such that their filters are continued instead of being restarted. Two devices stabilize the search. First, candidates are evaluated with coupled Monte Carlo draws through common random numbers, which reduces the variance of pairwise score differences. Second, the search region is repeatedly recentered and rescaled around the best configuration found so far. Numerical experiments on a linear random-walk model and the nonlinear Lorenz-63 and Lorenz-96 systems showed that the configuration selected by PRS is close to the seed-averaged exhaustive-grid optimum – on one task, its single-run evaluation exceeds the seed-averaged grid-best score – while using approximately 2 %–25 % of the cost of grid search. The largest absolute computational saving was achieved on the high-dimensional Lorenz-96 model.

title: RSIA: Defending Against Dynamic Collusive Attacks in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning, unlike centralized training, enables multiple clients to train a global model without exposing raw data, making it useful for applications such as medical diagnosis in smart healthcare and mobile edge networks. This setting is vulnerable to dynamic collusive attacks, where colluding clients coordinate abnormal parameter updates and adjust their strategies across training rounds. Existing studies address this problem with isolated mechanisms that focus on a single defense stage, but such mechanisms are insufficient for attacks that evolve across rounds. To address this challenge, we propose reputation-aware Stackelberg incentive aggregation (RSIA) to mitigate the influence of dynamic collusive attacks while balancing model utility in federated learning. Specifically, we first use incentive rules before local training to make repeated collusive behavior less beneficial. We then update client reputation after each round, so earlier unreliable behavior affects later incentives. Finally, we use reputation and update reliability to weight client updates, reducing the influence of abnormal updates on global model training. Experiments on three datasets show that RSIA reduces the average effective attack success rate by 84.9% compared with representative state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. RSIA also maintains competitive test accuracy, providing a favorable trade-off between model utility and attack suppression.

title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning Models for Autonomous Resource Optimization
abstract: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning (ARL) has become a paradigm shift of autonomous optimization of resources in dynamic and uncertain settings.The conventional management methods of resources are based on inflexible models and rule-based decision making systems which are not responsive to the environmental changes, system needs or operational limitations.Adaptive reinforcement learning models deal with such constraints by allowing systems to adopt optimal resource allocation policies by a continuous interaction with the environment, adaptation through feedback and long run optimization of rewards.The models are especially useful when working with such systems as smart grids, autonomous vehicles, cloud computing, smart agriculture, and intelligent infrastructure systems.ARL ensures the efficient use of the computational, energy, and physical resources through the introduction of adaptive learning mechanisms, multi-agent coordination, and real-time optimization of decisions.Recent progress in deep reinforcement learning, multi-agent reinforcement learning as well as hybrid intelligent frameworks has greatly contributed in increasing the scale, convergence rate and accuracy of decisions.Besides, the incorporation with edge computing, digital twins, and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies allows managing the resources in a decentralized and autonomous way.This paper provides an in-depth review of adaptive reinforcement learning frameworks in the context of autonomous resource optimization, their approaches, functionality, and industrial use.Experimental evidence has shown that learning about adaptive reinforcement has great efficacy in streamlining processes and operating at a lower cost, the system remains stable and autonomous decision making with complex resource management settings is successful.

title: Integrated CAV Agent Architectures with MCP and A2A
abstract: This chapter establishes theoretical foundations and practical frameworks for building unified agent systems that seamlessly integrate the model context protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent protocol (A2A) in connected and autonomous vehicle (CAV) applications. Real-world CAV applications demand unified systems combining external capabilities with collaborative reasoning. The chapter covers protocol selection criteria, system architectures for protocol integration, and implementation guidelines for robust systems operating in safety-critical environments. It examines how integrated architectures enable CAVs to access both deterministic external services and collaborative peer intelligence, addressing complex decision-making scenarios requiring both tool integration and multi-agent coordination. The chapter provides comprehensive guidance for building and deploying integrated agent systems in CAV environments.

title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
abstract: Chatbot Arena ranks language models with the Bradley-Terry model, which gives each model one score and so assumes Luce's choice axiom. Choice theory predicts where this fails: near-copies are told apart more decisively than their scores imply. On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley-Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later gives consistent multipliers, and the effect survives alternative tie treatments, prompt subsets and topics, and timing checks. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. A correction with four to six parameters predicts held-out votes better than Bradley-Terry and than models with hundreds of parameters, mostly by modelling ties; frozen and carried to new releases in a test fixed in advance, its gains are concentrated in ties, and better head-to-head odds are not established. The leaderboard order barely moves. With language-model judges and three-answer menus, a near-copy takes votes mostly from its twin when choices are pooled over prompts (log-odds shift +0.10, 95% interval 0.05 to 0.16); within a prompt the shift is smaller and clear for two of four judges.

title: Dual-Domain Sparse-View 4D CBCT Reconstruction with Spatial-Temporal Consistency Learning
abstract: Four-dimensional cone-beam computed tomography (4D CBCT) provides phase-resolved volumetric images for image-guided radiotherapy. Yet good reconstruction quality usually needs many projections. This increases scan time and radiation dose. We propose STCNet, a sparse-view 4D CBCT reconstruction framework that uses spatial-temporal consistency learning. STCNet reconstructs high-quality images from only 16 projections in each respiratory phase. STCNet integrates physics-driven positional encoding to enforce geometric consistency in the projection domain and introduces temporal encoding in latent space to capture respiratory motion dynamics across phases to capture dynamic respiratory motion across phases. A dual-domain collaborative strategy jointly optimizes both projection and image domains, enhancing structural fidelity and temporal coherence. We tested STCNet on the TCIA-LUNG dataset and a CIRS thorax phantom dataset. STCNet performed better than conventional methods and recent deep learning baselines in image quality, artifact reduction, and structural preservation. On TCIA-LUNG, STCNet reached PSNR values of 33.311, 32.695, and 32.658 dB at phases 2, 5, and 8. The corresponding SSIM values were 0.845, 0.823, and 0.825. On CIRS, STCNet achieved PSNR values up to 36.497 dB and SSIM values up to 0.877. These results support STCNet as a promising framework for low-dose, phase-resolved 4D CBCT reconstruction in image-guided radiotherapy.

title: More Reader Data or a Better Teacher? Updating a Model of Crowd Highlights in Late 2026
abstract: A model trained on readers' highlights can show a newcomer where earlier readers converged on a page, even on pages with few readers. A year of stronger language models suggests two upgrades: use them directly, or use them as teachers. We compare both with a third, more reader data, on one social highlighting platform, with the comparisons, the selection rules and a sealed set of fresh pages fixed in advance. On 215 development pages, seven language models released by October 2026 rank sentences zero-shot at an average precision of at most 0.3744 against the sentences half the readers marked most, and 0.3931 when fused with reading position, while a 3-billion-parameter model trained on reader highlights alone reaches 0.4346. Used as the teacher that breaks ties among readers' counts, the stronger fusion changes a trained model by +0.0013 [-0.0012, +0.0040], whereas going from half to all of its training pages adds +0.0242 [+0.0179, +0.0301]. A 27-billion-parameter backbone on the reader-only recipe adds +0.0225 on the development pages; on 131 fresh pages, read once and too few for a confirmatory comparison, its difference from the 3-billion model is unresolved, both score above the fusion, and in an exploratory split their lead over the previous model sits on pages from domains that their fresh training pages also cover. In this recipe, more reader data improves a trained model where a stronger tie-breaking teacher yields no material gain, and frontier models used as rankers still trail a small model trained on readers.

title: Analisis Sentimen Program MBG Sebelum Dan Sesudah Implementasi Pada Platform X Dan Tiktok Menggunakan SVM
abstract: Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) merupakan kebijakan pemerintah Indonesia untuk menanggulangi stunting melalui penyediaan asupan gizi. Sebagai program nasional, MBG memunculkan beragam respons publik yang banyak disampaikan melalui media sosial. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis perubahan sentimen publik sebelum dan setelah implementasi MBG pada platform X dan TikTok, serta mengevaluasi kinerja metode Support Vector Machine (SVM). Data dikumpulkan melalui scraping menggunakan tagar #MakanSiangGratis, #MakanBergiziGratis, dan #MBG, dengan total 4.000 data pada masing-masing platform untuk periode sebelum dan sesudah implementasi. Tahapan penelitian meliputi pelabelan sentimen, preprocessing, pembobotan TF-IDF, dan klasifikasi menggunakan SVM dengan evaluasi K-Fold Cross Validation. Hasil menunjukkan perbedaan pola sentimen setelah implementasi. Pada platform X, sentimen negatif meningkat dan positif menurun, sedangkan di TikTok sentimen positif tetap dominan meskipun netral dan negatif meningkat. Secara keseluruhan, SVM menunjukkan kinerja yang baik dan stabil dengan tingkat akurasi tinggi, serta memberikan kontribusi akademik dalam kajian analisis sentimen kebijakan publik di media sosial.Kata kunci: Analisis Sentimen; MBG; Platform TikTok; Platform X; Support Vector Machine
